sentences.zh: 【後唐紀八】 起閼逢敦牂二月，盡旃蒙協洽，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Tang Annals 8] From the second month of Emao Dunzhang through Zhanmeng Xiehe; a little more than one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Tang Annals 8] From the second month of Emao Dunzhang through Zhanmeng Xiehe—a little more than one year in all.

sentences.zh: 潞王下清泰元年（

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Lu, the first year of Qingtai (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Lu, the first year of Qingtai (

sentences.zh: 甲午，公元九三四年）

translations.literal: Jiawu, AD 934)
translations.idiomatic: Jiawu, AD 934)

sentences.zh: 二月，癸酉，蜀主以武泰節度使趙季良為司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事，領節度使如故。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day Guiyou, the ruler of Shu appointed Wutai Military Commissioner Zhao Jiliang Grand Master of Works and concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Grand Councillor, retaining his commissionership as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day Guiyou, the ruler of Shu appointed Zhao Jiliang, military commissioner of Wutai, Grand Master of Works and concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Grand Councillor, while he continued to hold his commissionership.

sentences.zh: 吳人多不欲遷都者，都押牙周宗言於徐知誥曰：「主上西遷，公復須東行，不惟勞費甚大，且違眾心。」

translations.literal: Many in Wu did not wish to move the capital; Capital Guard Zhou Zong said to Xu Zhigao, "When the sovereign moves west, you will have to travel east again—not only will the labor and expense be very great, but it will also go against the people's wishes."
translations.idiomatic: Many people in Wu opposed moving the capital. Zhou Zong, chief of the capital guard, said to Xu Zhigao, "When the sovereign moves west, you will have to travel east again. That would not only cost a great deal in labor and expense but also run counter to popular sentiment."

sentences.zh: 丙子，吳主遣宋齊丘如金陵，諭知誥罷遷都。

translations.literal: On the day Bingzi, the ruler of Wu sent Song Qiqiu to Jinling to instruct Zhigao to abandon the plan to move the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingzi, the ruler of Wu sent Song Qiqiu to Jinling to tell Zhigao to abandon the plan to move the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，知誥久有傳禪之志，以吳主無失德，恐眾心不悅，欲待嗣君；

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhigao had long harbored the wish to receive the abdication of the throne; because the ruler of Wu had committed no fault, he feared the people would not be pleased and wished to wait for the heir;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhigao had long wished to receive the throne by abdication. Because the ruler of Wu had done nothing wrong, he feared the people would not accept it and intended to wait for the heir.

sentences.zh: 宋齊丘亦以為然。

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu also thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu agreed.

sentences.zh: 一旦，知誥臨鏡鑷白髭，歎曰：「國家安而吾老矣，奈何？」

translations.literal: One day Zhigao, facing the mirror plucking white whiskers, sighed and said, "The state is secure and I am old—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: One day Zhigao stood before the mirror plucking out white whiskers and sighed, "The realm is at peace and I am growing old. What am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 周宗知其意，請如江都，微以傳禪諷吳主，且告齊丘。

translations.literal: Zhou Zong understood his intent, asked to go to Jiangdu, and subtly hinted to the ruler of Wu about the abdication, and also informed Qiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zong understood what he meant, asked to go to Jiangdu, and subtly suggested abdication to the ruler of Wu; he also informed Qiqiu.

sentences.zh: 齊丘以宗先己，心疾之，遣使馳詣金陵，手書切諫，以為天時人事未可；

translations.literal: Qiqiu, because Zong had acted before him, resented him in his heart; he sent a messenger posthaste to Jinling with a personal letter urgently remonstrating that the times and human affairs were not yet ripe;
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu resented Zong for having acted first. He sent a messenger posthaste to Jinling with a personal letter urgently advising that the times and circumstances were not yet right.

sentences.zh: 知誥愕然。

translations.literal: Zhigao was startled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao was taken aback.

sentences.zh: 後數日，齊丘至，請斬宗以謝吳主，乃黜宗為池州副使。

translations.literal: Several days later Qiqiu arrived, asked that Zong be executed to apologize to the ruler of Wu, and Zong was demoted to deputy commissioner of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Qiqiu arrived and asked that Zong be executed to appease the ruler of Wu. Zong was instead demoted to deputy commissioner of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，節度副使李建勳、行軍司馬徐玠等屢陳知誥功業，宜早從民望，召宗復為都押牙。

translations.literal: After a long while, Deputy Commissioner Li Jianxun, Campaigning Army Marshal Xu Jie, and others repeatedly stated Zhigao's achievements and that he should early follow the people's hopes; Zong was recalled as chief of the capital guard.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, Deputy Commissioner Li Jianxun, Campaigning Army Marshal Xu Jie, and others repeatedly urged that Zhigao's achievements entitled him to meet the people's hopes at once. Zong was recalled as chief of the capital guard.

sentences.zh: 知誥由是疏齊丘。

translations.literal: Zhigao thereby grew distant from Qiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: From this Zhigao grew estranged from Qiqiu.

sentences.zh: 朱弘昭、馮贇不欲石敬瑭久在太原，且欲召孟漢瓊，己卯，徙成德節度使范延光為天雄節度使，代漢瓊；

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun did not wish Shi Jingtang to remain long at Taiyuan and also wished to recall Meng Hanqiong; on the day Jimao, Chengde Military Commissioner Fan Yanguang was transferred to Tianxiong Military Commissioner in Hanqiong's place;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun did not want Shi Jingtang to remain long at Taiyuan and also wished to recall Meng Hanqiong. On the day Jimao, Fan Yanguang, military commissioner of Chengde, was transferred to Tianxiong to replace Hanqiong.

sentences.zh: 徙潞王從珂為河東節度使，兼北都留守；

translations.literal: the Prince of Lu Congke was transferred to Hedong Military Commissioner, concurrently Northern Capital regent;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Lu, Congke, was transferred to military commissioner of Hedong and concurrently regent of the Northern Capital;

sentences.zh: 徙石敬瑭為成德節度使。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang was transferred to Chengde Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: and Shi Jingtang was transferred to military commissioner of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 皆不降制書，但各遣使臣持宣監送赴鎮。

translations.literal: In none of these cases was an edict issued; each was simply sent to his post by envoys bearing imperial pronouncements to supervise the transfer.
translations.idiomatic: No formal edicts were issued for any of these moves; envoys bearing imperial pronouncements were simply sent to escort each man to his new post.

sentences.zh: 吳主詔徐知誥還府捨。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu ordered Xu Zhigao to return to his official residence.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu ordered Xu Zhigao to return to his official residence.

sentences.zh: 甲申，金陵大火；

translations.literal: On the day Jiashen a great fire broke out in Jinling;
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiashen a great fire broke out in Jinling;

sentences.zh: 乙酉，又火。

translations.literal: on the day Yiyou there was fire again.
translations.idiomatic: on the day Yiyou there was fire again.

sentences.zh: 知誥疑有變，勒兵自衛。

translations.literal: Zhigao suspected a coup and mustered troops to guard himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao suspected treachery and mustered troops to guard himself.

sentences.zh: 己丑，復入府捨。

translations.literal: On the day Jichou he returned to his official residence.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jichou he returned to his official residence.

sentences.zh: 潞王既與朝廷猜阻，朝廷又命洋王從璋權知鳳翔。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu, already mutually suspicious with the court, was further ordered by the court to have Prince of Yang Congzhang act as provisional administrator of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu was already at odds with the court through mutual suspicion, and the court now ordered Prince of Yang Congzhang to serve provisionally as administrator of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 從璋性粗率樂禍，前代安重誨鎮河中，欲殺之；

translations.literal: Congzhang was coarse and rash by nature and delighted in misfortune; when formerly An Chonghui governed Hezhong, he had wished to kill him;
translations.idiomatic: Congzhang was coarse and rash by nature and took pleasure in others' misfortune. When An Chonghui had earlier governed Hezhong, Congzhang had wished to kill him.

sentences.zh: 潞王聞其來，尤惡之，欲拒命則兵弱糧少，不知所為，謀於將佐，皆曰：「主上富於春秋，政事出於朱、馮，大王功名震主，離鎮必無全理，不可受也。」

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu heard he was coming, he hated it all the more; if he wished to refuse the order his troops were few and grain scant, and he did not know what to do. He consulted his generals and aides, who all said, "The sovereign is still young in years; government affairs proceed from Zhu and Feng. Your Highness's achievements and fame overshadow the throne—if you leave your commission you will certainly not survive whole; you must not accept."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu heard that Congzhang was coming, he hated the move all the more. If he refused the order his forces were weak and supplies few, and he did not know what to do. He consulted his generals and staff, who all said, "The sovereign is still young, and government is in the hands of Zhu and Feng. Your Highness's fame and achievements overshadow the throne. If you leave your post you will surely not survive. You must not accept."

sentences.zh: 王問觀察判官滴河馬胤孫曰：「今道過京師，當何向為便？」

translations.literal: The prince asked Observation Commissioner Ma Yinsun of Dihe, "If I now pass through the capital on the way, which route would be best?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked Ma Yinsun, observation commissioner of Dihe, "If I now pass through the capital on the way, which course would be best?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「君命召，不俟駕。

translations.literal: He replied, "When the ruler's command summons, one does not wait for the carriage to be ready.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "When the ruler summons, one does not wait for the carriage to be ready.

sentences.zh: 臨喪赴鎮，又何疑焉！

translations.literal: To attend a funeral and proceed to your commission—what is there to doubt!
translations.idiomatic: To attend a funeral and proceed to your post—what is there to doubt!

sentences.zh: 諸人凶謀，不可從也。」

translations.literal: The others' wicked schemes must not be followed."
translations.idiomatic: The others' wicked schemes must not be followed."

sentences.zh: 眾哂之。

translations.literal: The assembly sneered at him.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly sneered at him.

sentences.zh: 王乃移檄鄰道，言「朱弘昭等乘先帝疾亟，殺長立少，專制朝權，別疏骨肉，動搖籓垣，懼傾覆社稷。

translations.literal: The prince then issued a proclamation to neighboring circuits, saying, "Zhu Hongzhao and others, taking advantage of the late emperor's grave illness, killed the elder to install the younger, monopolized court power, estranged kin, shook the frontier defenses, and feared to overturn the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then issued a proclamation to neighboring circuits, saying, "Zhu Hongzhao and others, taking advantage of the late emperor's grave illness, killed the elder to install the younger, monopolized court power, estranged the imperial kin, and shook the frontier defenses, threatening to overturn the realm.

sentences.zh: 今從珂將入朝以清君側之惡，而力不能獨辦，願乞靈鄰籓以濟之。」

translations.literal: Now Congke will enter court to purge the evil at the ruler's side, but his strength cannot accomplish it alone; I beg the spiritual aid of neighboring commissions to bring it to completion."
translations.idiomatic: Now Congke will enter court to purge the evil at the ruler's side, but he cannot accomplish this alone. I beg neighboring commissions for their aid to bring it to completion."

sentences.zh: 潞王以西都留守王思同當東出之道，尤欲與之相結，遣推官郝詡、押牙朱廷乂等相繼詣長安，說以利害，餌以美妓，不從則令就圖之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu, because Western Capital Regent Wang Sitong stood in the path eastward, especially wished to win him over; he sent Administrative Aide Hao Xu, Guard Officer Zhu Tingyi, and others in succession to Chang'an to persuade him with advantage and harm, bait him with beautiful courtesans, and if he would not comply, have him disposed of.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu especially wished to win over Wang Sitong, regent of the Western Capital, who stood in the path eastward. He sent Administrative Aide Hao Xu, Guard Officer Zhu Tingyi, and others in succession to Chang'an to persuade him with promises and threats, bait him with beautiful courtesans, and have him killed if he would not comply.

sentences.zh: 思同謂將吏曰：「吾受明宗大恩，今與鳳翔同反，借使事成而榮，猶為一時之叛臣，況事敗而辱，流千古之丑跡乎！」

translations.literal: Sitong said to his generals and officials, "I received great favor from Emperor Mingzong; now to rebel with Fengxiang—even if the affair succeeded and brought glory, I would still be a rebel for a time; how much more if it failed and brought shame, leaving an ugly mark through the ages!"
translations.idiomatic: Sitong said to his generals and officials, "I received great favor from Emperor Mingzong. To rebel now with Fengxiang—even if the affair succeeded and brought glory, I would still be a rebel for a time. How much worse if it failed and brought shame, leaving an ugly mark for all ages!"

sentences.zh: 遂執詡等，以狀聞。

translations.literal: He thereupon seized Xu and the others and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon seized Xu and the others and reported the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 時潞王使者多為鄰道所執，不則依阿操兩端，惟隴州防禦使相裡金傾心附之，遣判官薛文遇往來計事。

translations.literal: At this time most of the Prince of Lu's envoys were seized by neighboring circuits, or else vacillated between two sides; only Longzhou Defense Commissioner Xiangli Jin gave him his whole heart, sending Administrative Aide Xue Wenyü back and forth to plan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At this time most of the Prince of Lu's envoys were seized by neighboring circuits, or else hedged between two sides. Only Xiangli Jin, defense commissioner of Longzhou, gave him his whole-hearted support and sent Administrative Aide Xue Wenyü back and forth to plan affairs.

sentences.zh: 金，并州人也。

translations.literal: Jin was a man of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was a native of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議討鳳翔。

translations.literal: The court deliberated on punishing Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The court deliberated on punishing Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 康義誠不欲出外，恐失軍權，請以王思同為統帥，以羽林都指揮使侯益為行營馬步軍都虞侯。

translations.literal: Kang Yicheng did not wish to go out, fearing loss of military authority, and asked that Wang Sitong be made commander-in-chief and Imperial Guard Commander Hou Yi made campaigning army horse-and-foot deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yicheng did not wish to leave the capital, fearing loss of military authority, and asked that Wang Sitong be made commander-in-chief and Imperial Guard Commander Hou Yi made deputy commander of the campaigning horse-and-foot forces.

sentences.zh: 益知軍情將變，辭疾不行。

translations.literal: Yi knew the army's temper was about to change and pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yi knew the army's temper was about to change and pleaded illness to avoid going.

sentences.zh: 執政怒之，出為商州刺史。

translations.literal: The chief ministers were angry and transferred him out as prefect of Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were angry and transferred him out as prefect of Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以王思同為西面行營馬步軍都部署，前靜難節度使藥彥稠副之，前絳州刺吏萇從簡為馬步都虞候，嚴衛步軍左廂指揮使尹暉、羽林指揮使楊思權等皆為偏裨。

translations.literal: On the day Xinmao Wang Sitong was made Western Campaigning Army horse-and-foot commander-in-chief, former Jingnan Military Commissioner Yao Yanchou his deputy, former Jiangzhou Prefect Chang Congjian horse-and-foot deputy commander, and Left Wing Commander of the Strict Guard Foot Army Yin Hui, Imperial Guard Commander Yang Siquan, and others all subordinate commanders.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinmao, Wang Sitong was made commander-in-chief of the western campaigning horse-and-foot forces, with former Jingnan Military Commissioner Yao Yanchou as his deputy, former Jiangzhou Prefect Chang Congjian as deputy commander, and Left Wing Commander of the Strict Guard Foot Army Yin Hui, Imperial Guard Commander Yang Siquan, and others as subordinate commanders.

sentences.zh: 暉，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Hui was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀主以中門使王處回為樞密使。

translations.literal: The ruler of Shu appointed Inner Gate Commissioner Wang Chuhui Palace Secretariat Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Shu appointed Inner Gate Commissioner Wang Chuhui Palace Secretariat Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，加王思同同平章事，知鳳翔行府；

translations.literal: On the day Dingyou Wang Sitong was given the additional title Co-Grand Councillor and made administrator of the Fengxiang campaigning headquarters;
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dingyou, Wang Sitong was given the additional title Co-Grand Councillor and made administrator of the Fengxiang campaigning headquarters;

sentences.zh: 以護國節度使安彥威為西面行營都監。

translations.literal: Huguo Military Commissioner An Yanwei was made Western Campaigning Army overseer.
translations.idiomatic: and Huguo Military Commissioner An Yanwei was made overseer of the western campaigning army.

sentences.zh: 思同雖有忠義之志，而御軍無法；

translations.literal: Although Sitong had a loyal and righteous will, he had no method of commanding troops;
translations.idiomatic: Although Sitong was loyal and righteous in intent, he had no method of commanding troops.

sentences.zh: 潞王老於行陣，將士徼幸富貴者心皆向之。

translations.literal: the Prince of Lu was old in battle lines, and soldiers who hoped for wealth and rank all turned their hearts toward him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu was experienced in battle, and soldiers who hoped for wealth and rank all turned their hearts toward him.

sentences.zh: 詔遣殿直楚匡祚執亳州團練使李重吉，幽於宋州。

translations.literal: An edict sent Palace Attendant Chu Kuangzuo to seize Bozhou Training Commissioner Li Chongji and imprison him at Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Palace Attendant Chu Kuangzuo to seize Li Chongji, training commissioner of Bozhou, and imprison him at Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 洋王從璋行至關西，聞鳳翔拒命而還。

translations.literal: Prince of Yang Congzhang, traveling as far as Guanxi, heard that Fengxiang had refused the order and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yang Congzhang, traveling as far as Guanxi, heard that Fengxiang had refused the order and turned back.

sentences.zh: 三月，安彥威與山南西道張虔釗、武定孫漢韶、彰義張從賓、靜難康福等五節度使奏合兵討鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the third month, An Yanwei together with Shannan West Circuit Zhang Qianzhao, Wuding Sun Hanshao, Zhangyi Zhang Congbin, Jingnan Kang Fu, and four other military commissioners memorialized to combine forces and punish Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, An Yanwei together with Zhang Qianzhao of Shannan West Circuit, Sun Hanshao of Wuding, Zhang Congbin of Zhangyi, Kang Fu of Jingnan, and four other military commissioners memorialized to combine forces and punish Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 漢韶，李存進之子也。

translations.literal: Hanshao was the son of Li Cunjin.
translations.idiomatic: Hanshao was the son of Li Cunjin.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，諸道兵大集於鳳翔城下攻之，克東西關城，城中死者甚眾。

translations.literal: On the day Yimao the armies of all circuits massed below Fengxiang city and attacked; they took the eastern and western gate cities, and very many died in the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yimao the armies of all circuits massed below Fengxiang and attacked. They took the eastern and western gate cities, and very many died within the city.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，復進攻城，期於必取。

translations.literal: On the day Bingchen they advanced again to attack the city, expecting to take it without fail.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingchen they advanced again to attack the city, determined to take it.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔城塹卑淺，守備俱乏，眾心危急，潞王登城泣謂外軍曰：「吾未冠從先帝百戰，出入生死，金創滿身，以立今日之社稷；

translations.literal: Fengxiang's moat was low and shallow, its defenses all lacking, and hearts in the city were desperate. The Prince of Lu ascended the wall weeping and said to the armies outside, "Before I came of age I followed the late emperor through a hundred battles, in and out of life and death, my body covered with wounds of metal, to establish today's altars of state;
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang's moat was low and shallow, its defenses were lacking, and hearts in the city were desperate. The Prince of Lu ascended the wall weeping and said to the armies outside, "Before I came of age I followed the late emperor through a hundred battles, in and out of life and death, my body covered with wounds, to help establish today's realm.

sentences.zh: 汝曹從我，目睹其事。

translations.literal: you followed me and witnessed these things with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: You followed me and witnessed these things with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷信任讒臣，猜忌骨肉，我何罪而受誅乎！」

translations.literal: Now the court trusts slanderous ministers and is suspicious of kin—what crime have I committed to deserve execution!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the court trusts slanderous ministers and is suspicious of its own kin. What crime have I committed to deserve execution!"

sentences.zh: 因慟哭。

translations.literal: He thereupon wailed bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon wailed bitterly.

sentences.zh: 聞者哀之。

translations.literal: Those who heard were moved to pity.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 張虔釗性褊急，主攻城西南，以白刃驅士卒登城，士卒怒，大詬，反攻之，虔釗躍馬走免，楊思權因大呼曰：「大相公，吾主也。」

translations.literal: Zhang Qianzhao was narrow and impatient by nature; he chiefly attacked the southwest of the city and drove the soldiers up the wall with naked blades. The soldiers grew angry and cursed loudly, then turned and attacked him; Qianzhao leaped on his horse and fled. Yang Siquan thereupon shouted loudly, "The Great Lord is my sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qianzhao was narrow and impatient by nature. He chiefly attacked the southwest of the city and drove the soldiers up the wall at sword point. The soldiers grew angry, cursed loudly, and turned on him. Qianzhao leaped on his horse and fled. Yang Siquan thereupon shouted, "The Great Lord is my sovereign."

sentences.zh: 遂帥諸軍解甲投兵，請降於潞王，自西門入，以幅紙進潞王曰：「願王克京城日，以臣為節度使，勿以為防、團。」

translations.literal: He thereupon led the armies to doff armor and cast down weapons, requesting surrender to the Prince of Lu; entering by the western gate, he presented a strip of paper to the prince saying, "When Your Highness takes the capital, make me military commissioner—do not appoint me defense or training commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon led the armies to doff armor and cast down weapons and surrender to the Prince of Lu. Entering by the western gate, he presented a strip of paper to the prince saying, "When Your Highness takes the capital, make me military commissioner—do not appoint me to a defense or training post."

sentences.zh: 潞王即書「思權可邠寧節度使」授之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu immediately wrote "Siquan may be Binning Military Commissioner" and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu immediately wrote "Siquan may be military commissioner of Binning" and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 王思同猶未之知，趣士卒登城，尹暉大呼曰：「城西軍已入城受賞矣。」

translations.literal: Wang Sitong still did not know of it and urged the soldiers up the wall. Yin Hui shouted loudly, "The army on the west of the city has already entered the city and received rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sitong still did not know of it and urged the soldiers up the wall. Yin Hui shouted loudly, "The army on the west of the city has already entered the city and received rewards."

sentences.zh: 眾爭棄甲投兵而降，其聲震地。

translations.literal: The masses vied to cast off armor and weapons and surrender; the sound shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: The masses vied to cast off armor and weapons and surrender. The sound shook the earth.

sentences.zh: 日中，亂兵悉入，外軍亦潰，思同等六節度使皆遁去。

translations.literal: At midday the disorderly troops had all entered; the outer armies also collapsed, and Sitong and the other six military commissioners all fled.
translations.idiomatic: By midday the disorderly troops had all entered the city. The outer armies also collapsed, and Sitong and the other six military commissioners all fled.

sentences.zh: 潞王悉斂城中將吏士民之財以犒軍，至於鼎釜皆估直以給之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu gathered all the wealth of generals, officials, soldiers, and commoners in the city to reward the army, even to the point of appraising cauldrons and pots to distribute their value.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu gathered all the wealth of generals, officials, soldiers, and commoners in the city to reward the army, even appraising cauldrons and pots to distribute their value.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，王思同、藥彥稠等走至長安，西京副留守劉遂雍閉門不內，乃趣潼關。

translations.literal: On the day Dingsi Sitong, Yao Yanchou, and others fled as far as Chang'an; Western Capital Deputy Regent Liu Suiyong closed the gates and would not admit them, and they hastened toward Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dingsi, Sitong, Yao Yanchou, and others fled as far as Chang'an. Liu Suiyong, deputy regent of the Western Capital, closed the gates and would not admit them, and they hastened toward Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 遂雍，鄩之子也。

translations.literal: Suiyong was the son of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Suiyong was the son of Ye.

sentences.zh: 潞王建大將旗鼓，整眾而東，以孔目官虞城劉延朗為腹心。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu raised great general's banners and drums, put his forces in order, and marched east, taking Clerk Liu Yanlang of Yucheng as his intimate confidant.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu raised great general's banners and drums, put his forces in order, and marched east, taking Clerk Liu Yanlang of Yucheng as his intimate confidant.

sentences.zh: 潞王始憂王思同等並力據長安拒守，至岐山，聞劉遂雍不內思同，甚喜，遣使慰撫之，遂雍悉出府庫之財於外，軍士前至者即給賞令過；

translations.literal: The prince had at first worried that Sitong and the others would combine forces to hold Chang'an and resist; when he reached Qishan and heard that Liu Suiyong would not admit Sitong, he was greatly pleased, sent envoys to comfort and reassure him. Suiyong brought out all the wealth of the treasury outside the walls; soldiers who arrived first were immediately given rewards and told to pass on;
translations.idiomatic: The prince had at first worried that Sitong and the others would combine forces to hold Chang'an and resist. When he reached Qishan and heard that Liu Suiyong would not admit Sitong, he was greatly pleased and sent envoys to comfort and reassure him. Suiyong brought out all the wealth of the treasury outside the walls; soldiers who arrived first were immediately given rewards and told to pass on.

sentences.zh: 比潞王到，前軍賞遍，皆不入城。

translations.literal: by the time the Prince of Lu arrived, the vanguard had been rewarded throughout and none entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the Prince of Lu arrived, the vanguard had been rewarded throughout and none entered the city.

sentences.zh: 庚申，潞王至長安，遂雍迎謁，率民財以充賞。

translations.literal: On the day Gengshen the Prince of Lu reached Chang'an; Suiyong came out to meet and pay respects, leading the people's wealth to fill out the rewards.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengshen the Prince of Lu reached Chang'an. Suiyong came out to meet and pay respects, leading the people's wealth to fill out the rewards.

sentences.zh: 是日，西面步軍都監王景從等自軍前奔還，中外大駭。

translations.literal: That day Western Foot Army Overseer Wang Jingcong and others fled back from the front; inside and outside the court were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: That day Wang Jingcong, overseer of the western foot army, and others fled back from the front. Court and country were greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 帝不知所為，謂康義誠等曰：「先帝棄萬國，朕外守籓方，當是之時，為嗣者在諸公所取耳，朕實無心與人爭國。

translations.literal: The emperor did not know what to do and said to Kang Yicheng and the others, "The late emperor abandoned the myriad states; I guarded a frontier commission abroad. At that time the successor was whom you gentlemen chose—I truly had no mind to contend for the realm with anyone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not know what to do and said to Kang Yicheng and the others, "When the late emperor died I was guarding a frontier post abroad. At that time the successor was whom you gentlemen chose. I truly had no wish to contend for the realm with anyone.

sentences.zh: 既承大業，年在幼沖，國事皆委諸公。

translations.literal: Once I undertook the great enterprise, my years were still tender; state affairs were all entrusted to you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Once I undertook the throne my years were still tender, and state affairs were all entrusted to you gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 朕于兄弟間不至榛梗，諸公以社稷大計見告，朕何敢違！

translations.literal: Between me and my brothers there was no thorn or stem; when you gentlemen informed me of the great plan for the altars of state, how dared I disobey!
translations.idiomatic: Between me and my brothers there was no estrangement. When you gentlemen informed me of the great plan for the realm, how could I disobey!

sentences.zh: 軍興之初，皆自誇大，以為寇不足平；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the campaign you all boasted yourselves, thinking the rebel insufficient to subdue;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the campaign you all boasted that the rebel could easily be subdued.

sentences.zh: 今事至於此，何方可以轉禍？

translations.literal: now matters have come to this—by what means can disaster be turned?
translations.idiomatic: Now matters have come to this. By what means can disaster be turned?

sentences.zh: 朕欲自迎潞王，以大位讓之，若不免於罪，亦所甘心。」

translations.literal: I wish to go myself to welcome the Prince of Lu and yield the great throne to him; if I cannot escape guilt, that too I would accept willingly."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to go myself to welcome the Prince of Lu and yield the throne to him. If I cannot escape guilt, I would accept that willingly."

sentences.zh: 朱弘昭、馮贇大懼，不敢對。

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun were greatly afraid and dared not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun were greatly afraid and dared not reply.

sentences.zh: 義誠欲悉以宿衛兵迎降為己功，乃曰：「西師驚潰，蓋主將失策耳。

translations.literal: Yicheng wished to take all the palace guard to welcome the surrender as his own achievement and therefore said, "The western army collapsed in panic—this was merely the chief commander's loss of strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng wished to take all the palace guard to welcome the surrender as his own achievement and therefore said, "The western army collapsed in panic—this was merely the chief commander's failure of strategy.

sentences.zh: 今侍衛諸軍尚多，臣請自往扼其衝要，招集離散以圖後效，幸陛下勿為過憂！」

translations.literal: The palace guard armies are still many; I beg to go myself to hold their vital points, gather the scattered, and plan for later effect—may Your Majesty not be overly troubled!"
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard armies are still numerous. I beg to go myself to hold their vital points, gather the scattered, and plan for later effect. May Your Majesty not be overly troubled!"

sentences.zh: 帝遣使召石敬瑭，欲令將兵拒之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to summon Shi Jingtang, wishing to have him lead troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to summon Shi Jingtang, wishing to have him lead troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 義誠固請自行，帝乃召將士慰諭，空府庫以勞之，許以平鳳翔，人更賞二百緡，府庫不足，當以宮中服玩繼之。

translations.literal: Yicheng firmly asked to go himself; the emperor then summoned generals and soldiers to comfort and instruct them, emptied the treasury to reward them, promised that on pacifying Fengxiang each man would receive two hundred strings of cash more; when the treasury was insufficient, palace robes and curios would follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng firmly asked to go himself. The emperor then summoned generals and soldiers to comfort and instruct them, emptied the treasury to reward them, and promised that on pacifying Fengxiang each man would receive two hundred strings of cash more. When the treasury was insufficient, palace robes and curios would follow.

sentences.zh: 軍士益驕，無所畏忌，負賜物，揚言於路曰：「至鳳翔更請一分。」

translations.literal: The soldiers grew all the more arrogant, fearless of nothing; bearing their gifts, they proclaimed along the road, "When we reach Fengxiang we shall ask for another share."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers grew all the more arrogant and fearless. Bearing their gifts, they proclaimed along the road, "When we reach Fengxiang we shall ask for another share."

sentences.zh: 遣楚匡祚殺李重吉於宋州；

translations.literal: He sent Chu Kuangzuo to kill Li Chongji at Songzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chu Kuangzuo to kill Li Chongji at Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 匡祚榜棰重吉，責其家財。

translations.literal: Kuangzuo posted a placard and flogged Chongji, demanding his family's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangzuo posted a placard and flogged Chongji, demanding his family's wealth.

sentences.zh: 又殺尼惠明。

translations.literal: He also killed the nun Huiming.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed the nun Huiming.

sentences.zh: 初，馬軍都指揮使朱洪實為秦王從榮所厚，及朱弘昭為樞密使，洪實以宗史事之；

translations.literal: Earlier, Horse Army Commander Zhu Hongshi had been favored by Prince of Qin Congrong; when Zhu Hongzhao became Palace Secretariat Commissioner, Hongshi treated him as a clansman in service;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Horse Army Commander Zhu Hongshi had been favored by Prince of Qin Congrong. When Zhu Hongzhao became Palace Secretariat Commissioner, Hongshi treated him as a kinsman in service.

sentences.zh: 從榮勒兵天津橋，洪實首為孟漢瓊擊從榮，康義誠由是恨之。

translations.literal: when Congrong mustered troops at Tianjin Bridge, Hongshi was the first to strike Congrong for Meng Hanqiong; Kang Yicheng therefore hated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Congrong mustered troops at Tianjin Bridge, Hongshi was the first to strike Congrong for Meng Hanqiong. Kang Yicheng therefore hated him.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，帝親至左藏，給將士金帛。

translations.literal: On the day Xinyou the emperor went in person to the Left Treasury and distributed gold and silks to the generals and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinyou the emperor went in person to the Left Treasury and distributed gold and silks to the generals and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 義誠、洪實共論用兵利害，洪實欲以禁軍固守洛陽，曰：「如此，彼亦未敢徑前，然後徐圖進取，可以萬全。」

translations.literal: Yicheng and Hongshi together discussed the advantages and harms of employing troops; Hongshi wished to have the forbidden army hold fast at Luoyang and said, "In this way they also will not dare advance directly; then we may slowly plan advance and seizure—it can be wholly secure."
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng and Hongshi together discussed military strategy. Hongshi wished to have the forbidden army hold fast at Luoyang and said, "In this way they also will not dare advance directly. Then we may slowly plan advance and seizure. That would be wholly secure."

sentences.zh: 義誠怒曰：「洪實為此言，欲反邪！」

translations.literal: Yicheng angrily said, "Hongshi speaks thus—does he wish to rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng angrily said, "Hongshi speaks thus—does he wish to rebel!"

sentences.zh: 洪實曰：「公自欲反，乃謂誰反！」

translations.literal: Hongshi said, "You yourself wish to rebel—whom else do you call rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Hongshi said, "You yourself wish to rebel—whom else do you call rebel!"

sentences.zh: 其聲漸厲。

translations.literal: Their voices gradually grew fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Their voices gradually grew fierce.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，召而訊之，二人訟於帝前，帝不能辨其是非，遂斬洪實，軍士益憤怒。

translations.literal: The emperor heard, summoned and questioned them; the two disputed before the emperor, and the emperor could not distinguish right from wrong—thereupon Hongshi was executed, and the soldiers grew all the more angry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard, summoned and questioned them. The two disputed before the emperor, and the emperor could not distinguish right from wrong. Thereupon Hongshi was executed, and the soldiers grew all the more angry.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，潞王至昭應，聞前軍獲王思同，王曰：「思同雖失計，然盡心所奉，亦可嘉也。」

translations.literal: On the day Renxu the Prince of Lu reached Zhaoying; hearing that the vanguard had captured Wang Sitong, the prince said, "Although Sitong lost his strategy, yet he gave his whole heart to whom he served—this too may be praised."
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renxu the Prince of Lu reached Zhaoying. Hearing that the vanguard had captured Wang Sitong, the prince said, "Although Sitong lost his strategy, he gave his whole heart to whom he served. That too may be praised."

sentences.zh: 癸亥，至靈口，前軍執思同以至，王責讓之，對曰：「思同起行間，先帝擢之，位至節將，常愧無功以報大恩。

translations.literal: On the day Guihai he reached Lingkou; the vanguard brought Sitong forward. The prince rebuked him, and he replied, "Sitong rose from the ranks; the late emperor promoted him to the rank of commissioner, and I have always been ashamed of having no achievement with which to repay great favor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guihai he reached Lingkou. The vanguard brought Sitong forward. The prince rebuked him, and he replied, "I rose from the ranks. The late emperor promoted me to the rank of commissioner, and I have always been ashamed of having no achievement with which to repay his great favor.

sentences.zh: 非不知附在王立得富貴，助朝廷自取禍殃，但恐死之日無面目見先帝於泉下耳。

translations.literal: It is not that I did not know that siding with Your Highness would bring wealth and rank, or that aiding the court would bring disaster on myself—but I feared that on the day of my death I would have no face to meet the late emperor beneath the springs.
translations.idiomatic: I knew that siding with Your Highness would bring wealth and rank, and that aiding the court would bring disaster on myself. But I feared that on the day of my death I would have no face to meet the late emperor in the underworld.

sentences.zh: 敗而釁鼓，固其所也。

translations.literal: To be defeated and smeared on the war drum is what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: To be defeated and smeared on the war drum is only what I deserve.

sentences.zh: 請早就死！」

translations.literal: I beg to die soon!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg to die at once!"

sentences.zh: 王為之改容，曰：「公且休矣。」

translations.literal: The prince changed countenance for him and said, "Sir, rest for now."
translations.idiomatic: The prince's expression softened, and he said, "Sir, rest for now."

sentences.zh: 王欲宥之，而楊思權之徒恥見其面。

translations.literal: The prince wished to spare him, but Yang Siquan and his sort were ashamed to see his face.
translations.idiomatic: The prince wished to spare him, but Yang Siquan and his followers were ashamed to see his face.

sentences.zh: 王之過長安，尹暉盡取思同家資及妓妾，屢言於劉延朗曰：「若留思同，慮失士心。」

translations.literal: When the prince passed Chang'an, Yin Hui took all of Sitong's family wealth and courtesans, and repeatedly said to Liu Yanlang, "If Sitong is kept, I fear we will lose the soldiers' hearts."
translations.idiomatic: When the prince passed Chang'an, Yin Hui seized all of Sitong's family wealth and courtesans and repeatedly said to Liu Yanlang, "If we keep Sitong, I fear we will lose the soldiers' hearts."

sentences.zh: 屬王醉，不待報，擅殺思同及其妻子。

translations.literal: When the prince was drunk, without awaiting reply he on his own authority killed Sitong and his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was drunk, without awaiting reply he killed Sitong and his wife and children on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 王醒，怒延朗，嗟惜者累日。

translations.literal: When the prince awoke, he was angry with Yanlang and sighed in regret for many days.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince awoke, he was angry with Yanlang and sighed in regret for many days.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，制以康義誠為鳳翔行營都招討使，以王思同副之。

translations.literal: On the day Guihai an edict made Kang Yicheng Fengxiang Campaigning Headquarters Grand Pacification Commissioner, with Wang Sitong as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guihai an edict made Kang Yicheng Grand Pacification Commissioner of the Fengxiang campaigning headquarters, with Wang Sitong as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 甲子，潞王至華州，獲藥彥稠，囚之。

translations.literal: On the day Jiazi the Prince of Lu reached Huazhou, captured Yao Yanchou, and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiazi the Prince of Lu reached Huazhou, captured Yao Yanchou, and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，至閿鄉。

translations.literal: On the day Yichou he reached Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yichou he reached Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷前後所發諸軍，遇西軍皆迎降，無一人戰者。

translations.literal: The armies the court had sent out before and after, encountering the western army, all welcomed and surrendered; not one man fought.
translations.idiomatic: Every army the court had sent out, when it met the western forces, welcomed them and surrendered. Not a single man fought.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，康義誠引侍衛兵發洛陽，詔以侍衛馬軍指揮使安從進為京城巡檢；

translations.literal: On the day Bingyin Kang Yicheng led the palace guard out of Luoyang; an edict made Palace Guard Horse Army Commander An Congjin capital inspector;
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingyin Kang Yicheng led the palace guard out of Luoyang. An edict made Palace Guard Horse Army Commander An Congjin capital inspector.

sentences.zh: 從進已受潞王書，潛布腹心矣。

translations.literal: Congjin had already received a letter from the Prince of Lu and secretly planted trusted agents.
translations.idiomatic: Congjin had already received a letter from the Prince of Lu and secretly planted trusted agents.

sentences.zh: 是日，潞王至靈寶，護國節度使安彥威、匡國節度使安重霸皆降，惟保義節度使康思立謀固守陝城以俟康義誠。

translations.literal: That day the Prince of Lu reached Lingbao; Huguo Military Commissioner An Yanwei and Kuangguo Military Commissioner An Chongba both surrendered; only Baoyi Military Commissioner Kang Sili planned to hold fast at Shan city and await Kang Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Prince of Lu reached Lingbao. An Yanwei of Huguo and An Chongba of Kuangguo both surrendered. Only Kang Sili of Baoyi planned to hold Shan city and await Kang Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，捧聖五百騎戍陝西，為潞王前鋒，至城下，呼城上人曰：「禁軍十萬已奉新帝，爾輩數人奚為！

translations.literal: Earlier, five hundred Pingsheng cavalry garrisoned Shanxi as the Prince of Lu's vanguard; reaching below the city, they called to those above, "A hundred thousand forbidden troops have already received the new emperor—what are you few doing!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, five hundred Pingsheng cavalry garrisoned Shanxi as the Prince of Lu's vanguard. Reaching below the city, they called to those above, "A hundred thousand forbidden troops have already received the new emperor. What are you few doing!

sentences.zh: 徒累一城人塗地耳。」

translations.literal: You will only bring the whole city's people to ruin on the ground."
translations.idiomatic: You will only bring the whole city's people to ruin."

sentences.zh: 於是捧聖卒爭出迎，思立不能禁，不得已亦出迎。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Pingsheng soldiers vied to go out and welcome them; Sili could not restrain them and, having no choice, also went out to welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Pingsheng soldiers vied to go out and welcome them. Sili could not restrain them and, having no choice, also went out to welcome.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，潞王至陝，僚佐說王曰：「今大王將及京畿，傳聞乘輿已播遷，大王宜少留於此，先移書慰安京城士庶。」

translations.literal: On the day Dingmao the Prince of Lu reached Shan; his aides said to the prince, "Now Your Highness is about to reach the capital region; it is rumored the imperial carriage has already fled. Your Highness should pause here a little and first send a letter to comfort and reassure the officials and commoners of the capital."
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dingmao the Prince of Lu reached Shan. His aides said, "Your Highness is about to reach the capital region, and it is rumored the imperial carriage has already fled. You should pause here and first send a letter to comfort the officials and commoners of the capital."

sentences.zh: 王從之，移書諭洛陽文武士庶，惟朱弘昭、馮贇兩族不赦外，自餘勿有憂疑。

translations.literal: The prince followed this advice and sent a proclamation instructing Luoyang's civil and military officials and commoners that except for the two clans of Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun, who would not be pardoned, the rest should have no worry or doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The prince followed this advice and sent a proclamation to Luoyang's civil and military officials and commoners. Except for the clans of Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun, who would not be pardoned, the rest should have no worry or doubt.

sentences.zh: 康義誠軍至新安，所部將士自相結，百什為群，棄甲兵，爭先詣陝降，纍纍不絕。

translations.literal: When Kang Yicheng's army reached Xin'an, his generals and soldiers bound themselves together in groups of tens and hundreds, cast off armor and weapons, and vied to go to Shan to surrender in an unbroken stream.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Yicheng's army reached Xin'an, his generals and soldiers bound themselves together in groups of tens and hundreds, cast off armor and weapons, and vied to go to Shan to surrender in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 義誠至干壕，麾下才數十人；

translations.literal: Yicheng reached Ganhao with only several dozen men under him;
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng reached Ganhao with only several dozen men under him.

sentences.zh: 遇潞王侯騎十餘人，義誠解所佩弓劍為信，因侯騎請降於潞王。

translations.literal: he met a dozen or so of the Prince of Lu's outriders; Yicheng unfastened the bow and sword he wore as tokens of trust and through the outriders requested surrender to the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He met a dozen or so of the Prince of Lu's outriders. Yicheng unfastened the bow and sword he wore as tokens of trust and through the outriders requested surrender to the Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，閔帝聞潞王至陝，義誠軍潰，憂駭不知所為，急遣中使召朱弘昭謀所向，弘昭曰：「急召我，欲罪之也。」

translations.literal: On the day Wuchen Emperor Min heard the Prince of Lu had reached Shan and Yicheng's army had collapsed; alarmed and at a loss, he urgently sent a palace envoy to summon Zhu Hongzhao to plan their course. Hongzhao said, "An urgent summons means he wishes to punish me."
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuchen Emperor Min heard the Prince of Lu had reached Shan and Yicheng's army had collapsed. Alarmed and at a loss, he urgently sent a palace envoy to summon Zhu Hongzhao to plan their course. Hongzhao said, "An urgent summons means he wishes to punish me."

sentences.zh: 赴井死。

translations.literal: He threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 安從進聞弘昭死，殺馮贇於第，滅其族，傳弘昭、贇首於潞王。

translations.literal: An Congjin, hearing of Hongzhao's death, killed Feng Yun at his residence, exterminated his clan, and sent the heads of Hongzhao and Feng to the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: An Congjin, hearing of Hongzhao's death, killed Feng Yun at his residence, exterminated his clan, and sent the heads of Hongzhao and Feng to the Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 帝欲奔魏州，召孟漢瓊使詣魏州為先置；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to flee to Weizhou and summoned Meng Hanqiong to go to Weizhou to make preparations in advance;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to flee to Weizhou and summoned Meng Hanqiong to go to Weizhou to make preparations in advance.

sentences.zh: 漢瓊不應召，單騎奔陝。

translations.literal: Hanqiong did not answer the summons and rode alone to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Hanqiong did not answer the summons and rode alone to Shan.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在籓鎮，愛信牙將慕容遷，及即位，以為控鶴指揮使；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was in his frontier commission, he loved and trusted Guard General Murong Qian; when he took the throne he made him Crane-Control Commander;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor was in his frontier commission, he loved and trusted Guard General Murong Qian. When he took the throne he made him Crane-Control Commander.

sentences.zh: 帝將北渡河，密與之謀，使帥部兵守玄武門。

translations.literal: when the emperor was about to cross the river north, he secretly plotted with him and had him lead his troops to guard the Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to cross the river north, he secretly plotted with Qian and had him lead his troops to guard the Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝以五十騎出玄武門，謂遷曰：朕且幸魏州，徐圖興復，汝帥有馬控鶴從我。」

translations.literal: That evening the emperor with fifty horsemen went out the Xuanwu Gate and said to Qian, "I am about to travel in favor to Weizhou and slowly plan restoration. You lead the mounted Crane-Control and follow me."
translations.idiomatic: That evening the emperor with fifty horsemen went out the Xuanwu Gate and said to Qian, "I am about to travel to Weizhou and slowly plan restoration. You lead the mounted Crane-Control and follow me."

sentences.zh: 遷曰：「生死從大家。」

translations.literal: Qian said, "In life or death I follow Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "In life or death I follow Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 乃陽為團結；

translations.literal: He then pretended to muster them;
translations.idiomatic: He then pretended to muster them.

sentences.zh: 帝既出，即闔門不行。

translations.literal: once the emperor had gone out, he closed the gate and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had gone out, he closed the gate and would not go.

sentences.zh: 己巳，馮道等入朝，及端門，聞朱、馮死，帝已北走。

translations.literal: On the day Jisi Feng Dao and others entered court; reaching the Duan Gate, they heard Zhu and Feng were dead and the emperor had already fled north.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jisi Feng Dao and others entered court. Reaching the Duan Gate, they heard Zhu and Feng were dead and the emperor had already fled north.

sentences.zh: 道及劉昫欲歸，李愚曰：「天子之出，吾輩不預謀。

translations.literal: Dao and Liu Xu wished to return home; Li Yu said, "The sovereign's departure—we were not party to the planning.
translations.idiomatic: Dao and Liu Xu wished to return home. Li Yu said, "The sovereign's departure—we were not party to the planning.

sentences.zh: 今太后在宮，吾輩當至中書，遣小黃門取太后進止，然後歸第，人臣之義也。」

translations.literal: Now the empress dowager is in the palace; we should go to the Secretariat, send a junior palace attendant to obtain the empress dowager's decision, and then return to our residences—that is the duty of subjects."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager is still in the palace. We should go to the Secretariat, send a junior palace attendant to obtain her decision, and then return to our residences. That is the duty of subjects."

sentences.zh: 道曰：「主上失守社稷，人臣惟君是奉，無君而入宮城，恐非所宜。

translations.literal: Dao said, "The sovereign has lost the altars of state; subjects serve only the ruler. To enter the palace city without a ruler—I fear that is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Dao said, "The sovereign has lost the realm. Subjects serve only the ruler. To enter the palace city without a ruler—I fear that is not fitting.

sentences.zh: 潞王已處處張榜，不若歸俟教令。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu has posted proclamations everywhere; better to return home and await his instructions."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu has posted proclamations everywhere. Better to return home and await his instructions."

sentences.zh: 乃歸。

translations.literal: They then returned.
translations.idiomatic: They then returned.

sentences.zh: 至天宮寺，安從進遣人語之曰：「潞王倍道而來，且至矣，相公宜帥百官至谷水奉迎。」

translations.literal: Reaching Tiangong Temple, An Congjin sent someone to tell them, "The Prince of Lu is coming by double marches and will soon arrive; the chief ministers should lead the hundred officials to Gushui to welcome him."
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Tiangong Temple, An Congjin sent someone to tell them, "The Prince of Lu is coming by forced marches and will soon arrive. The chief ministers should lead the hundred officials to Gushui to welcome him."

sentences.zh: 乃止於寺中，召百官。

translations.literal: They then stopped at the temple and summoned the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: They then stopped at the temple and summoned the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人盧導至，馮道曰：「俟舍人久矣，所急者勸進文書，宜速具草。」

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Lu Dao arrived; Feng Dao said, "I have waited long for the drafter; what is urgent is the document urging accession—you should quickly prepare a draft."
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafter Lu Dao arrived. Feng Dao said, "I have waited long for you. What is urgent is the document urging accession. You should quickly prepare a draft."

sentences.zh: 導曰：「潞王入朝，百官班迎可也；

translations.literal: Dao said, "When the Prince of Lu enters court, the hundred officials may line up to welcome him;
translations.idiomatic: Dao said, "When the Prince of Lu enters court, the hundred officials may line up to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 設有廢立，當俟太后教令，豈可遽議勸進乎？」

translations.literal: if there is to be deposition and installation, we should await the empress dowager's instruction—how can we hastily discuss urging accession?"
translations.idiomatic: If there is to be deposition and installation, we should await the empress dowager's instruction. How can we hastily discuss urging accession?"

sentences.zh: 道曰：「事當務實。」

translations.literal: Feng Dao said, "Affairs must be handled practically."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said, "Affairs must be handled practically."

sentences.zh: 導曰：「安有天子在外，人臣遽以大位勸人者邪！

translations.literal: Lu Dao said, "How can there be subjects who hastily urge the great throne on someone while the Son of Heaven is outside!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dao said, "How can subjects hastily urge the throne on someone while the Son of Heaven is outside!

sentences.zh: 若潞王守節北面，以大義見責，將何辭以對！

translations.literal: If the Prince of Lu holds to his duty facing north and reproaches us with great righteousness, with what words shall we answer!
translations.idiomatic: If the Prince of Lu holds to his duty facing north and reproaches us with righteousness, with what words shall we answer!

sentences.zh: 公不如帥百官詣宮門，進名問安，取太后進止，則去就善矣。」

translations.literal: You would do better to lead the hundred officials to the palace gate, present your names to inquire after her health, and obtain the empress dowager's decision—then going or staying would be well settled."
translations.idiomatic: You would do better to lead the hundred officials to the palace gate, present your names to inquire after her health, and obtain the empress dowager's decision. Then going or staying would be well settled."

sentences.zh: 道未及對，從進屢遣人趣之曰：「潞王至矣，太后、太妃已遣中使迎勞矣，安得百官無班！」

translations.literal: Before Feng Dao could reply, Congjin repeatedly sent men to urge them, saying, "The Prince of Lu has arrived; the empress dowager and imperial consort have already sent palace envoys to welcome and comfort him—how can the hundred officials have no formation!"
translations.idiomatic: Before Feng Dao could reply, Congjin repeatedly sent men to urge them, saying, "The Prince of Lu has arrived. The empress dowager and imperial consort have already sent palace envoys to welcome him. How can the hundred officials have no formation!"

sentences.zh: 道等即紛然而去。

translations.literal: Dao and the others at once scattered and went.
translations.idiomatic: Dao and the others at once scattered and went.

sentences.zh: 既而潞王未至，三相息於上陽門外，盧導過於前，道復召而語之，導對如初。

translations.literal: After a while the Prince of Lu had not yet arrived; the three chief ministers rested outside the Shangyang Gate. Lu Dao passed before them; Feng Dao again summoned and spoke with him, and Dao answered as before.
translations.idiomatic: After a while the Prince of Lu had not yet arrived. The three chief ministers rested outside the Shangyang Gate. Lu Dao passed before them. Feng Dao again summoned and spoke with him, and Dao answered as before.

sentences.zh: 李愚曰：「舍人之言是也。

translations.literal: Li Yu said, "The drafter's words are right.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu said, "The drafter is right.

sentences.zh: 吾輩之罪，擢發不足數。」

translations.literal: Our crimes—even plucking hair could not count them."
translations.idiomatic: Our crimes—even counting them hair by hair would not suffice."

sentences.zh: 康義誠至陝等罪，潞王責之曰：「先帝晏駕，立嗣在諸公；

translations.literal: When Kang Yicheng reached Shan and the like to answer for his crimes, the Prince of Lu reproached him, saying, "When the late emperor passed away, establishing the heir lay with you gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Yicheng reached Shan to answer for his crimes, the Prince of Lu reproached him, saying, "When the late emperor passed away, establishing the heir lay with you gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 今上亮陰，政事出諸公，何為不能終始，陷吾弟至此乎？」

translations.literal: the present sovereign is in mourning; government affairs proceed from you gentlemen—why could you not see it through from start to finish and have trapped my younger brother to this point?"
translations.idiomatic: The present sovereign is in mourning, and government affairs proceed from you gentlemen. Why could you not see it through from start to finish and have trapped my younger brother to this point?"

sentences.zh: 義誠大懼，叩頭請死。

translations.literal: Yicheng was greatly afraid, knocked his head and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng was greatly afraid, knocked his head, and begged for death.

sentences.zh: 王素惡其為人，未欲遽誅，且宥之。

translations.literal: The prince had always hated his character and did not wish to execute him hastily; for the time being he pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had always hated his character and did not wish to execute him hastily. For the time being he pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 馬步都虞侯萇從簡、左龍武統軍王景戡皆為部下所執，降於潞王，東軍盡降。

translations.literal: Horse-and-foot Deputy Commander Chang Congjian and Left Dragon Martial Commander Wang Jingzhan were both seized by their subordinates and surrendered to the Prince of Lu; the eastern armies all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Horse-and-foot Deputy Commander Chang Congjian and Left Dragon Martial Commander Wang Jingzhan were both seized by their subordinates and surrendered to the Prince of Lu. The eastern armies all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 潞王上箋於太后取進止，遂自陝而東。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu submitted a memorial to the empress dowager to obtain her decision, then marched east from Shan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu submitted a memorial to the empress dowager to obtain her decision, then marched east from Shan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚午朔，未明，閔帝至衛州東數里，遇石敬瑭；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day Gengwu, before dawn Emperor Min reached several li east of Weizhou and met Shi Jingtang;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day Gengwu, before dawn Emperor Min reached several li east of Weizhou and met Shi Jingtang.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，問以社稷大計，敬瑭曰：「聞康義誠西討，何如？

translations.literal: the emperor was greatly pleased and asked him about the great plan for the altars of state. Jingtang said, "I heard Kang Yicheng was campaigning west—how did it go?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and asked him about the great plan for the realm. Jingtang said, "I heard Kang Yicheng was campaigning west. How did it go?

sentences.zh: 陛下何為至此？」

translations.literal: Why has Your Majesty come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Why has Your Majesty come to this?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「義誠亦叛去矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Yicheng has also rebelled and gone."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yicheng has also rebelled and gone."

sentences.zh: 敬瑭俯首長歎數四，曰：「衛州刺史王弘贄，宿將習事，請與圖之。」

translations.literal: Jingtang bowed his head and sighed long several times, saying, "Weizhou Prefect Wang Hongzan is an old general experienced in affairs; please let me consult with him."
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang bowed his head and sighed long several times. "Weizhou Prefect Wang Hongzan is an old general experienced in affairs. Please let me consult with him."

sentences.zh: 乃往見弘贄問之，弘贄曰：「前代天子播遷多矣，然皆有將相、侍衛、府庫、法物，使群下有所瞻仰；

translations.literal: He then went to see Hongzan and ask him. Hongzan said, "Former ages' Sons of Heaven who fled in exile were many, yet all had generals and ministers, guards, treasuries, and ritual objects, so that subordinates had something to look up to;
translations.idiomatic: He then went to see Hongzan and ask him. Hongzan said, "Former ages' emperors who fled in exile were many, yet all had generals and ministers, guards, treasuries, and ritual objects, so that subordinates had something to look up to.

sentences.zh: 今皆無之，獨以五十騎自隨，雖有忠義之心，將若之何？」

translations.literal: now all these are lacking, and he follows himself with only fifty horsemen—even if there is a loyal and righteous heart, what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Now all these are lacking, and he follows himself with only fifty horsemen. Even if there is a loyal and righteous heart, what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 敬瑭還，見帝於衛州驛，以弘贄之言告。

translations.literal: Jingtang returned and saw the emperor at the Weizhou post station, reporting Hongzan's words.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang returned and saw the emperor at the Weizhou post station and reported Hongzan's words.

sentences.zh: 弓箭庫使沙守榮、奔洪進前責敬瑭曰：「公明宗愛婿，富貴相與共之，憂患亦宜相恤。

translations.literal: Bow and Arrow Store Commissioner Sha Shourong and Ben Hongjin stepped forward and reproached Jingtang, saying, "You are Emperor Mingzong's beloved son-in-law; in wealth and rank you shared together, and in trouble you should also comfort each other.
translations.idiomatic: Bow and Arrow Store Commissioner Sha Shourong and Ben Hongjin stepped forward and reproached Jingtang. "You are Emperor Mingzong's beloved son-in-law. In wealth and rank you shared together, and in trouble you should also comfort each other.

sentences.zh: 今天子播越，委計於公，冀圖興復，乃以此四者為辭，是直欲附賊賣天子耳！」

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven is in exile and entrusts his plan to you, hoping to plot restoration—yet you take these four points as your excuse; this is plainly wishing to join the rebel and sell the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Today the Son of Heaven is in exile and entrusts his plan to you, hoping to plot restoration. Yet you take these four points as your excuse. This is plainly wishing to join the rebel and sell the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 守榮抽佩刀欲刺之，敬瑭親將陳暉救之，守榮與暉斗死，洪進亦自刎。

translations.literal: Shourong drew his girdle sword wishing to stab him; Jingtang's personal general Chen Hui rescued him; Shourong and Hui fought to the death, and Hongjin also cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Shourong drew his girdle sword to stab him. Jingtang's personal general Chen Hui rescued him. Shourong and Hui fought to the death, and Hongjin also cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭牙內指揮使劉知遠引兵入，盡殺帝左右及從騎，獨置帝而去。

translations.literal: Jingtang's Inner Guard Commander Liu Zhiyuan led troops in and killed all those at the emperor's side and his escort horsemen, leaving only the emperor and departing.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang's Inner Guard Commander Liu Zhiyuan led troops in and killed all those at the emperor's side and his escort horsemen, leaving only the emperor and departing.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭遂趣洛陽。

translations.literal: Jingtang then hastened to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang then hastened to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 是日，太后令內諸司至干壕迎潞王，王亟遣還洛陽。

translations.literal: That day the empress dowager ordered the inner palace offices to Ganhao to welcome the Prince of Lu; the prince quickly sent them back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That day the empress dowager ordered the inner palace offices to Ganhao to welcome the Prince of Lu. The prince quickly sent them back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 初，潞王罷河中，歸私第，王淑妃數遣孟漢瓊存撫之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Prince of Lu was dismissed from Hezhong and returned to his private residence, Consort Wang Shufei several times sent Meng Hanqiong to comfort and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Prince of Lu was dismissed from Hezhong and returned to his private residence, Consort Wang Shufei several times sent Meng Hanqiong to comfort and reassure him.

sentences.zh: 漢瓊自謂於王有舊恩，至澠池西，見王大哭，欲有所陳，王曰：「諸事不言可知。」

translations.literal: Hanqiong considered that he had old favor with the prince; west of Mianchi he saw the prince and wept greatly, wishing to say something. The prince said, "All matters need not be spoken to be known."
translations.idiomatic: Hanqiong considered that he had old favor with the prince. West of Mianchi he saw the prince and wept greatly, wishing to say something. The prince said, "All matters need not be spoken to be known."

sentences.zh: 仍自預從臣之列，王即命斬於路隅。

translations.literal: He still placed himself among the following ministers; the prince at once ordered him beheaded at the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: He still placed himself among the following ministers. The prince at once ordered him beheaded at the roadside.

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度使張虔釗之討鳳翔也，留武定節度使孫漢韶守興元。

translations.literal: When Shannan West Circuit Military Commissioner Zhang Qianzhao campaigned against Fengxiang, he left Wuding Military Commissioner Sun Hanshao to guard Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Qianzhao, military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, campaigned against Fengxiang, he left Sun Hanshao, military commissioner of Wuding, to guard Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 虔釗既敗，奔歸興元，與漢韶舉兩鎮之地降於蜀；

translations.literal: When Qianzhao was defeated he fled back to Xingyuan and, with Hanshao, offered the territory of both commissions in surrender to Shu;
translations.idiomatic: When Qianzhao was defeated he fled back to Xingyuan and, with Hanshao, offered the territory of both commissions in surrender to Shu.

sentences.zh: 蜀主命奉鑾肅衛馬步都指揮使、昭武節度使李肇將兵五千還利州，右匡聖馬步都指揮使、寧江節度使張業將兵一萬屯大漫天以迎之。

translations.literal: the ruler of Shu ordered Imperial Escort and Ceremonial Guard horse-and-foot Commander and Zhaowu Military Commissioner Li Zhao to lead five thousand troops back to Lizhou, and Right Kuangsheng horse-and-foot Commander and Ningjiang Military Commissioner Zhang Ye to lead ten thousand troops to garrison Datianmian to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Shu ordered Li Zhao, Imperial Escort and Ceremonial Guard horse-and-foot commander and military commissioner of Zhaowu, to lead five thousand troops back to Lizhou, and Zhang Ye, Right Kuangsheng horse-and-foot commander and military commissioner of Ningjiang, to lead ten thousand troops to garrison Datianmian to receive them.

sentences.zh: 壬申，潞王至蔣橋，百官班迎於路，傳教以未拜梓宮，未可相見。

translations.literal: On the day Renshen the Prince of Lu reached Jiangqiao; the hundred officials lined up on the road to welcome him. A message was transmitted that because he had not yet paid respects at the imperial coffin, he could not yet be received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renshen the Prince of Lu reached Jiangqiao. The hundred officials lined up on the road to welcome him. A message was transmitted that because he had not yet paid respects at the imperial coffin, he could not yet be received in audience.

sentences.zh: 馮道等皆上箋勸進。

translations.literal: Feng Dao and the others all submitted memorials urging accession.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao and the others all submitted memorials urging accession.

sentences.zh: 王入謁太后、太妃，詣西宮，伏梓宮慟哭，自陳詣闕之由。

translations.literal: The prince entered to pay respects to the empress dowager and imperial consort, went to the Western Palace, prostrated himself before the coffin and wailed bitterly, and stated on his own the reason for coming to court.
translations.idiomatic: The prince entered to pay respects to the empress dowager and imperial consort, went to the Western Palace, prostrated himself before the coffin and wailed bitterly, and stated the reason for coming to court.

sentences.zh: 馮道帥百官班見，王答拜。

translations.literal: Feng Dao led the hundred officials in formation to see him; the prince returned their bows.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao led the hundred officials in formation to see him. The prince returned their bows.

sentences.zh: 道等復上箋勸進，王立謂道等曰：「予之此行，事非獲已。

translations.literal: Dao and the others again submitted memorials urging accession. The prince stood and said to Dao and the others, "This journey of mine was not undertaken willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Dao and the others again submitted memorials urging accession. The prince stood and said to Dao and the others, "This journey of mine was not undertaken willingly.

sentences.zh: 俟皇帝歸闕，園寢禮終，當還守籓服，群公遽言及此，甚無謂也！」

translations.literal: Wait until the emperor returns to court and the rites at the imperial tomb are complete—I shall return to guard my frontier commission. For you gentlemen hastily to speak of this is very meaningless!"
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the emperor returns to court and the rites at the imperial tomb are complete. I shall return to guard my frontier commission. For you gentlemen hastily to speak of this is very meaningless!"

sentences.zh: 癸酉，太后下令廢少帝為鄂王，以潞王知軍國事，權以書詔印施行。

translations.literal: On the day Guiyou the empress dowager issued an order deposing the young emperor as Prince of E and making the Prince of Lu administrator of state and military affairs, provisionally using the written edict seal to put measures into effect.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guiyou the empress dowager issued an order deposing the young emperor as Prince of E and making the Prince of Lu administrator of state and military affairs, provisionally using the written edict seal to put measures into effect.

sentences.zh: 百官詣至德宮門待罪，王命各復其位。

translations.literal: The hundred officials went to the Gate of the Palace of Supreme Virtue to await punishment; the prince ordered each to resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials went to the Gate of the Palace of Supreme Virtue to await punishment. The prince ordered each to resume his post.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，太后令潞王宜即皇帝位；

translations.literal: On the day Jiaxu the empress dowager ordered that the Prince of Lu should immediately take the imperial throne;
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiaxu the empress dowager ordered that the Prince of Lu should immediately take the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，即位於柩前。

translations.literal: on the day Yihai he took the throne before the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yihai he took the throne before the coffin.

sentences.zh: 帝之發鳳翔也，許軍士以入洛人賞錢百緡。

translations.literal: When the emperor set out from Fengxiang he promised the soldiers a reward of a hundred strings of cash per man on entering Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor set out from Fengxiang he promised the soldiers a reward of a hundred strings of cash per man on entering Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 既至，問三司使王玫以府庫之實，對有數百萬在。

translations.literal: When he arrived he asked Three Departments Commissioner Wang Mei about the treasury's actual condition; he answered that several million were on hand.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he asked Three Departments Commissioner Wang Mei about the treasury's actual condition. Mei answered that several million were on hand.

sentences.zh: 既而閱實，金、帛不過三萬兩、匹；

translations.literal: When they then examined the actual amount, gold and silk amounted to no more than thirty thousand taels and bolts;
translations.idiomatic: When they then examined the actual amount, gold and silk amounted to no more than thirty thousand taels and bolts.

sentences.zh: 而賞軍之費計應用五十萬緡。

translations.literal: yet the cost of rewarding the army was calculated to require five hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the cost of rewarding the army was calculated to require five hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，玫請率京城民財以足之，數日，僅得數萬緡，帝謂執政曰：「軍不可不賞，人不可不恤，今將奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; Mei asked to lead the capital city's people's wealth to make it up. In several days they obtained only several tens of thousands of strings of cash. The emperor said to the chief ministers, "The army cannot go unrewarded, the people cannot go unrelieved—what is to be done now?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry. Mei asked to levy the capital city's people's wealth to make it up. In several days they obtained only several tens of thousands of strings of cash. The emperor said to the chief ministers, "The army cannot go unrewarded, the people cannot go unrelieved. What is to be done now?"

sentences.zh: 執政請據屋為率，無問士庶自居及僦者，預借五月僦直，從之。

translations.literal: The chief ministers asked to levy according to dwellings as the standard, without distinction between scholar and commoner, owner-occupier or renter, advancing five months' rent; this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers asked to levy according to dwellings as the standard, without distinction between scholar and commoner, owner-occupier or renter, advancing five months' rent. This was followed.

sentences.zh: 王弘贄遷閔帝於州廨，帝遣弘贄之子殿直巒往鴆之。

translations.literal: Wang Hongzan moved Emperor Min to the prefectural offices; the emperor sent Hongzan's son Palace Attendant Luan to poison him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongzan moved Emperor Min to the prefectural offices. The emperor sent Hongzan's son, Palace Attendant Luan, to poison him.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，巒至衛州謁見，閔帝問來故，不對。

translations.literal: On the day Wuyin, Luan arrived at Weizhou and paid his respects; Emperor Min asked the reason for his coming, and he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuyin, Luan arrived at Weizhou and paid his respects. Emperor Min asked why he had come, but Luan did not answer.

sentences.zh: 弘贄數進酒，閔帝知其有毒，不飲，巒縊殺之。

translations.literal: Hongzan repeatedly offered wine; Emperor Min knew it was poisoned and would not drink; Luan strangled him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzan repeatedly offered wine. Emperor Min knew it was poisoned and refused to drink, so Luan strangled him to death.

sentences.zh: 閔帝性仁厚，于兄弟敦睦，雖遭秦王忌疾，閔帝坦懷待之，卒免於患。

translations.literal: Emperor Min was by nature benevolent and generous; among his brothers he was affectionate and harmonious. Though the Prince of Qin bore him jealous ill will, Emperor Min treated him with open sincerity and in the end escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min was by nature benevolent and generous and affectionate toward his brothers. Though the Prince of Qin bore him jealous ill will, Emperor Min treated him with open sincerity and in the end escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，於潞王亦無嫌，而朱弘昭、孟漢瓊之徒橫生猜間，閔帝不能違，以致禍敗焉。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne he bore no ill will toward the Prince of Lu either, yet Zhu Hongzhao, Meng Hanqiong, and their like wantonly sowed suspicion between them. Emperor Min could not refuse them, and so met with disaster and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne he bore no ill will toward the Prince of Lu either, yet Zhu Hongzhao, Meng Hanqiong, and their like wantonly sowed suspicion between them. Emperor Min could not refuse them, and so met with disaster and ruin.

sentences.zh: 孔妃尚在宮中，王巒既還，潞王使人謂之曰：「重吉輩何在？」

translations.literal: Consort Kong was still in the palace. After Wang Luan returned, the Prince of Lu sent someone to say to her, "Where are Chongji and the others?"
translations.idiomatic: Consort Kong was still in the palace. After Wang Luan returned, the Prince of Lu sent someone to ask her, "Where are Chongji and the others?"

sentences.zh: 遂殺妃，並其四子。

translations.literal: He then killed the consort together with her four sons.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed the consort together with her four sons.

sentences.zh: 閔帝之在衛州也，惟磁州刺史宋令詢遣使問起居，聞其遇害，慟哭半日，自經死。

translations.literal: While Emperor Min was at Weizhou, only Cizhou Prefect Song Lingxun sent envoys to inquire after his health. When he heard that Min had been murdered, he wailed in grief for half a day and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Min was at Weizhou, only Cizhou Prefect Song Lingxun sent envoys to inquire after his health. When he heard that Min had been murdered, he wailed in grief for half a day and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 己卯，石敬瑭入朝。

translations.literal: On the day Jimao, Shi Jingtang entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jimao, Shi Jingtang came to court.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以劉昫判三司。

translations.literal: On the day Gengchen, Liu Xu was appointed to administer the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengchen, Liu Xu was appointed to administer the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，蜀在赦，改元明德。

translations.literal: On the day Xinsi, Shu proclaimed another amnesty and changed the era name to Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinsi, Shu proclaimed another amnesty and changed the era name to Mingde.

sentences.zh: 帝之起鳳翔也，召興州刺史劉遂清，遲疑不至。

translations.literal: When the emperor raised his forces at Fengxiang he summoned Xingzhou Prefect Liu Suiqing, but Suiqing hesitated and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor raised his forces at Fengxiang he summoned Xingzhou Prefect Liu Suiqing, but Suiqing hesitated and did not come.

sentences.zh: 聞帝入洛，乃悉集三泉、西縣、金牛、桑林戍兵以歸，自散關以南城鎮悉棄之，皆為蜀人所有。

translations.literal: When he heard that the emperor had entered Luoyang, he then gathered all the garrison troops of Sanquan, Xixian, Jinniu, and Sanglin and withdrew. From San Pass southward every fortified town was abandoned, and all fell into Shu hands.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that the emperor had entered Luoyang, he gathered all the garrison troops of Sanquan, Xixian, Jinniu, and Sanglin and withdrew. From San Pass southward every fortified town was abandoned, and all fell into Shu hands.

sentences.zh: 癸未，入朝，帝欲治其罪，以其能自歸，乃赦之。

translations.literal: On the day Guiwei he entered court. The emperor wished to punish him for his offense, but because he had come back of his own accord, he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guiwei he entered court. The emperor wished to punish him for his offense, but because he had returned of his own accord, he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 遂清。

translations.literal: Suiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Suiqing.

sentences.zh: 鄩之侄也。

translations.literal: He was the nephew of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He was the nephew of Li E.

sentences.zh: 甲申，蜀將張業將兵入興元、洋州。

translations.literal: On the day Jiashen, Shu general Zhang Ye led troops into Xingyuan and Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiashen, Shu general Zhang Ye led troops into Xingyuan and Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，改元，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day Yiyou, the era name was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yiyou, the era name was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以宣徽南院使郝瓊權判樞密院，前三司使王玫為宣徽北院使，鳳翔節度判官韓昭胤為左諫議大夫、充端明殿學士。

translations.literal: On the day Dinghai, Southern Palace Secretariat Commissioner Hao Qiong was appointed provisional administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs; former Three Departments Commissioner Wang Mei was made Northern Palace Secretariat Commissioner; and Fengxiang Military Commission administrative aide Han Zhaoyin was made Left Remonstrance Counselor and Academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dinghai, Hao Qiong, commissioner of the southern palace secretariat, was appointed provisional administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs; former Three Departments Commissioner Wang Mei was made commissioner of the northern palace secretariat; and Han Zhaoyin, administrative aide to the Fengxiang military commission, was made Left Remonstrance Counselor and Academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 戊子，斬河陽節度使、判六軍諸衛兼侍中康義誠，滅其族。
