translations.literal: On the day Wuzi, Heyang Military Commissioner and Administrator of the Six Armies and Various Guards, concurrently Palace Attendant Kang Yicheng, was executed and his clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuzi, Kang Yicheng, military commissioner of Heyang, administrator of the Six Armies and Various Guards, and concurrently palace attendant, was executed and his clan exterminated.

sentences.zh: 己丑，誅藥彥稠。

translations.literal: On the day Jichou, Yao Yanchou was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jichou, Yao Yanchou was put to death.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，釋王景戡、萇長簡。

translations.literal: On the day Gengyin, Wang Jingzhan and Chang Changjian were released.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengyin, Wang Jingzhan and Chang Changjian were released.

sentences.zh: 有司百方斂民財，僅得六萬，帝怒，下軍巡使獄，晝夜督責，囚系滿獄，貧者至自經、赴井。

translations.literal: The officials exhausted every means to levy the people's wealth and obtained only sixty thousand strings of cash. The emperor was angry and had them thrown into the military patrol commissioners' prison, where day and night they were pressed and held to account. The prisons filled with detainees, and the poor came even to hanging themselves or throwing themselves into wells.
translations.idiomatic: The officials exhausted every means to levy the people's wealth and obtained only sixty thousand strings of cash. The emperor was angry and had them thrown into the military patrol commissioners' prison, where day and night they were pressed and held to account. The prisons filled with detainees, and the poor came even to hanging themselves or throwing themselves into wells.

sentences.zh: 而軍士游市肆皆有驕色，市人聚詬之曰：「汝曹為主力戰，立功良苦，反使我輩鞭胸杖背，出財為賞，汝曹猶揚揚自得，獨不愧天地乎！」

translations.literal: Meanwhile soldiers strolling through the marketplaces all wore arrogant looks. The townspeople gathered and cursed them, saying, "You fought hard for your lord and toiled bitterly for merit, yet you have made us whipped on chest and back and pay out wealth for your rewards—and you still strut about pleased with yourselves. Are you alone without shame before Heaven and Earth?"
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile soldiers strolling through the marketplaces all wore arrogant looks. The townspeople gathered and cursed them, saying, "You fought hard for your lord and toiled bitterly for merit, yet you have made us whipped on chest and back and pay out wealth for your rewards—and you still strut about pleased with yourselves. Are you alone without shame before Heaven and Earth?"

sentences.zh: 是時，竭左藏舊物及諸道貢獻，乃至太后、太妃器服簪珥皆出之，才及二十萬緡，帝患之，李專美夜直，帝讓之曰：「卿名有才，不能為我謀此，留才安所施乎！」

translations.literal: At that time they exhausted the old stores of the Left Treasury and tribute from every circuit, even bringing out the empress dowager's and grand consort's vessels, robes, hairpins, and earrings, and still reached only two hundred thousand strings of cash. The emperor was distressed. Li Zhuanmei was on night duty at court, and the emperor reproached him, saying, "Your name means 'possessing talent,' yet you cannot plan this matter for me—where is talent to be applied if you keep it?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time they exhausted the old stores of the Left Treasury and tribute from every circuit, even bringing out the empress dowager's and grand consort's vessels, robes, hairpins, and earrings, and still reached only two hundred thousand strings of cash. The emperor was distressed. Li Zhuanmei was on night duty at court, and the emperor reproached him, saying, "Your name means 'possessing talent,' yet you cannot plan this matter for me—where is talent to be applied if you keep it?"

sentences.zh: 專美謝曰：「臣駑劣，陛下擢任過分，然軍賞不給，非臣之責也。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei apologized and said, "I am dull and inferior, and Your Majesty has promoted me beyond my deserts; yet that army rewards cannot be paid is not my responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei apologized and said, "I am dull and inferior, and Your Majesty has promoted me beyond my deserts; yet that army rewards cannot be paid is not my responsibility.

sentences.zh: 竊思自長興之季，賞賚亟行，卒以是驕；

translations.literal: I reflect that from the end of the Changxing era rewards and gifts were repeatedly issued, and the soldiers thereby grew arrogant;
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that from the end of the Changxing era rewards and gifts were repeatedly issued, and the soldiers thereby grew arrogant.

sentences.zh: 繼以山陵及出師，帑藏遂涸。

translations.literal: this was followed by the imperial tomb works and campaigns abroad, and the treasury was drained dry.
translations.idiomatic: This was followed by the imperial tomb works and campaigns abroad, and the treasury was drained dry.

sentences.zh: 雖有無窮之財，終不能滿驕卒之心，故陛下拱手於危困之中而得天下。

translations.literal: Even with inexhaustible wealth one could never satisfy the hearts of arrogant soldiers; that is why Your Majesty, hands folded in peril and distress, obtained the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Even with inexhaustible wealth one could never satisfy the hearts of arrogant soldiers; that is why Your Majesty, hands folded in peril and distress, obtained the realm.

sentences.zh: 夫國之存亡，不專繫於厚賞，亦在修法度，立紀綱。

translations.literal: A state's survival or ruin does not depend solely on lavish rewards; it also lies in repairing laws and institutions and establishing order and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: A state's survival or ruin does not depend solely on lavish rewards; it also lies in repairing laws and institutions and establishing order and discipline.

sentences.zh: 陛下苟不改覆車之轍，臣恐徒困百姓，存亡未可知也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will not turn from the track of the overturned cart, I fear you will only exhaust the common people, and survival or ruin will be impossible to know.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will not turn from the track of the overturned cart, I fear you will only exhaust the common people, and survival or ruin will be impossible to know.

sentences.zh: 今財力盡於此矣，宜據所有均給之，何必踐初言乎！」

translations.literal: Now financial strength is exhausted at this point; you ought to distribute evenly according to what is on hand—why must you keep your first promise!"
translations.idiomatic: Now financial strength is exhausted at this point; you ought to distribute evenly according to what is on hand—why must you keep your first promise!"

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought this right.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔禁軍在鳳翔歸命者，自楊思權、尹暉等各賜二馬、一駝、錢七十緡，下至軍人錢二十緡，其在京者各十緡。

translations.literal: On the day Renchen, an edict granted to palace guard troops at Fengxiang who had submitted, from Yang Siquan and Yin Hui downward, two horses, one camel, and seventy strings of cash each; common soldiers twenty strings of cash; and those in the capital ten strings each.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renchen, an edict granted to palace guard troops at Fengxiang who had submitted, from Yang Siquan and Yin Hui downward, two horses, one camel, and seventy strings of cash each; common soldiers twenty strings of cash; and those in the capital ten strings each.

sentences.zh: 軍士無厭，猶怨望，為謠言曰：「除去菩薩，扶立生鐵。」

translations.literal: The soldiers were insatiable and still resentful, and they made up a saying: "Remove the bodhisattva and install raw iron."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were insatiable and still resentful, and they made up a saying: "Remove the bodhisattva and install raw iron."

sentences.zh: 以閔帝仁弱，帝剛嚴，有悔心故也。

translations.literal: This was because Emperor Min had been benevolent and weak while the emperor was stern and severe, and they had regrets on that account.
translations.idiomatic: This was because Emperor Min had been benevolent and weak while the emperor was stern and severe, and they had regrets on that account.

sentences.zh: 丙申，葬聖德和武欽孝皇帝於徽陵，廟號明宗。

translations.literal: On the day Bingshen, the Sagely, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverent Filial Emperor was buried at Huiling; his temple name was Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingshen, the Sagely, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverent Filial Emperor was buried at Huiling; his temple name was Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 帝衰絰護從至陵所，宿焉。

translations.literal: The emperor, in mourning garments, escorted the procession to the tomb site and lodged there overnight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in mourning garments, escorted the procession to the tomb site and lodged there overnight.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙午，以韓昭胤為樞密使，以莊宅使劉延朗為樞密副使，權知樞密院記房暠為宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day Bingwu, Han Zhaoyin was made Commissioner of Military Affairs; Estate Commissioner Liu Yanlang was made Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs; and provisional Bureau of Military Affairs recorder Fang Gao was made Northern Palace Secretariat Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day Bingwu, Han Zhaoyin was made commissioner of military affairs; Estate Commissioner Liu Yanlang was made vice commissioner of military affairs; and Fang Gao, provisional recorder of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made commissioner of the northern palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 暠，長安人也。

translations.literal: Gao was a native of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was a native of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 帝與石敬瑭皆以勇力善鬥，事明宗為左右；

translations.literal: The emperor and Shi Jingtang were both skilled in courage and fighting strength and served Emperor Mingzong as his left and right hands;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Shi Jingtang were both skilled in courage and fighting strength and served Emperor Mingzong as his left and right hands.

sentences.zh: 然心競，素不相悅。

translations.literal: yet they rivaled each other in their hearts and had never been fond of one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they rivaled each other in their hearts and had never been fond of one another.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，敬瑭不得已入朝，山陵既畢，不敢言歸。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Jingtang had no choice but to enter court. After the tomb rites were completed, he did not dare speak of returning home.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Jingtang had no choice but to come to court. After the tomb rites were completed, he did not dare speak of returning home.

sentences.zh: 時敬瑭久病贏瘠，太后及魏國公主屢為之言；

translations.literal: At the time Jingtang had long been ill and was emaciated; the empress dowager and the Princess of Wei repeatedly spoke on his behalf;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jingtang had long been ill and was emaciated; the empress dowager and the Princess of Wei repeatedly spoke on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 而鳳翔舊將佐多勸帝留之，惟韓昭胤、李專美以為趙延壽在汴，不宜猜忌敬瑭。

translations.literal: yet many of the old Fengxiang generals and aides urged the emperor to keep him there. Only Han Zhaoyin and Li Zhuanmei held that with Zhao Yanshou at Bian, it was inappropriate to be suspicious of Jingtang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many of the old Fengxiang generals and aides urged the emperor to keep him there. Only Han Zhaoyin and Li Zhuanmei held that with Zhao Yanshou at Bian, it was inappropriate to be suspicious of Jingtang.

sentences.zh: 帝亦見其骨立，不以為虞，乃曰：「石郎不惟密親，兼自少與吾同艱難；

translations.literal: The emperor also saw how fleshless he was and did not regard him as a threat, and said, "Brother Stone is not only a close kinsman by marriage—since youth he has shared hardship with me;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also saw how emaciated he was and did not regard him as a threat, and said, "Brother Stone is not only a close kinsman by marriage—since youth he has shared hardship with me.

sentences.zh: 今我為天子，非石郎尚誰托哉！」

translations.literal: now that I am Son of Heaven, if not Brother Stone, on whom else should I rely!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am Son of Heaven, if not Brother Stone, on whom else should I rely!"

sentences.zh: 乃復以為河東節度使。

translations.literal: He then again appointed him Hedong Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He then again appointed him military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以隴州防禦使相裡金為保義節度使。

translations.literal: On the day Wuwu, Longzhou Defense Commissioner Xiangli Jin was made Baoyi Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuwu, Xiangli Jin, defense commissioner of Longzhou, was made military commissioner of Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 丁未，階州刺史趙澄降蜀。

translations.literal: On the day Dingwei, Jiezhou Prefect Zhao Cheng surrendered to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dingwei, Jiezhou Prefect Zhao Cheng surrendered to Shu.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以羽林軍使楊思權為靜難節度使。

translations.literal: On the day Wushen, Feathered Forest Army Commissioner Yang Siquan was made Jingnan Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wushen, Yang Siquan, commissioner of the Feathered Forest Army, was made military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 己酉，張虔釗、孫漢韶舉族遷於成都。

translations.literal: On the day Jiyou, Zhang Qianzhao and Sun Hanshao moved their entire clans to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiyou, Zhang Qianzhao and Sun Hanshao moved their entire clans to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事馮道同平章事，充匡國節度使。

translations.literal: On the day Gengxu, Grand Master of Works, concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Grand Councillor Feng Dao was made Co-Grand Councillor and appointed Kuangguo Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengxu, Feng Dao, grand master of works, concurrently vice director of the chancellery and co-grand councillor, was made co-grand councillor and appointed military commissioner of Kuangguo.

sentences.zh: 以天雄節度使兼侍中范延光為樞密使。

translations.literal: Tianxiong Military Commissioner, concurrently Palace Attendant Fan Yanguang was made Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang, military commissioner of Tianxiong and concurrently palace attendant, was made commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝之起鳳翔也，悉取天平節度使李從曮家財甲兵以供軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor raised his forces at Fengxiang, he took all the family wealth and armor and weapons of Tianping Military Commissioner Li Congyun to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor raised his forces at Fengxiang, he took all the family wealth and armor and weapons of Li Congyun, military commissioner of Tianping, to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 將行，鳳翔之民遮馬請復以從曮鎮鳳翔，帝許之，至是，徙從曮為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: When he was about to depart, the people of Fengxiang blocked his horse and asked that Congyun again be stationed at Fengxiang; the emperor agreed. At this time Congyun was transferred to be Fengxiang Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to depart, the people of Fengxiang blocked his horse and asked that Congyun again be stationed at Fengxiang; the emperor agreed. At this time Congyun was transferred to be military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 初，明宗為北面招討使，平盧節度使房知溫為副都部署，帝與別將事之，嘗被酒忿爭，拔刃相擬。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Mingzong was northern campaign commissioner-in-chief and Pinglu Military Commissioner Fang Zhiwen was deputy overall commander, the emperor and a separate general served under him. Once, drunk and angry, they quarreled and drew blades against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Mingzong was northern campaign commissioner-in-chief and Fang Zhiwen, military commissioner of Pinglu, was deputy overall commander, the emperor and a separate general served under him. Once, drunk and angry, they quarreled and drew blades against each other.

sentences.zh: 及帝舉兵入洛，知溫密與行軍司李沖謀拒之，沖請先奉表以觀形勢，還，言洛中已安定，知溫懼，壬戌，入朝謝罪，帝優禮之。

translations.literal: When the emperor raised troops and entered Luoyang, Zhiwen secretly plotted with campaign staff officer Li Chong to resist him. Chong asked first to submit a memorial to observe the situation; when he returned he said Luoyang was already settled. Zhiwen was afraid. On the day Renxu he entered court to apologize for his offense, and the emperor treated him with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor raised troops and entered Luoyang, Zhiwen secretly plotted with campaign staff officer Li Chong to resist him. Chong asked first to submit a memorial to observe the situation; when he returned he said Luoyang was already settled. Zhiwen was afraid. On the day Renxu he entered court to apologize for his offense, and the emperor treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 知溫貢獻甚厚。

translations.literal: Zhiwen's tribute gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen's tribute gifts were very generous.

sentences.zh: 吳鎮南節度使、守中書令東海康王徐知詢卒。

translations.literal: Wu Zhennan Military Commissioner, Guardian of the Secretariat, Prince Kang of Donghai Xu Zhixun died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhixun, Prince Kang of Donghai, military commissioner of Zhennan, guardian of the secretariat, died.

sentences.zh: 蜀人取成州。

translations.literal: Shu forces took Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shu forces took Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲戌，以皇子左衛上將軍重美為成德節度使、同平章事，兼河南尹，判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day Jiaxu, the emperor's son Left Guard General Chongmei was made Chengde Military Commissioner and Co-Grand Councillor, concurrently Henan Intendant, and Administrator of the Six Armies and Various Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day Jiaxu, the emperor's son Chongmei, Left Guard General, was made military commissioner of Chengde and co-grand councillor, concurrently intendant of Henan and administrator of the Six Armies and Various Guards.

sentences.zh: 文州都指揮使成延龜舉州附蜀。

translations.literal: Wenzhou Commander-in-Chief Cheng Yangui surrendered the prefecture to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yangui, commander-in-chief of Wenzhou, surrendered the prefecture to Shu.

sentences.zh: 吳徐知誥將受禪，忌照武節度使兼中書令臨川王濛，遣人告濛藏匿亡命，擅造兵器；

translations.literal: In Wu, Xu Zhigao was about to receive the abdication of the throne and resented Zhaowu Military Commissioner, concurrently Secretariat Director, Prince of Linchuan Meng. He sent men to accuse Meng of harboring fugitives and privately manufacturing weapons;
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Xu Zhigao was about to receive the abdication of the throne and resented Meng, Prince of Linchuan, military commissioner of Zhaowu and concurrently director of the secretariat. He sent men to accuse Meng of harboring fugitives and privately manufacturing weapons.

sentences.zh: 丙子，降封歷陽公，。

translations.literal: On the day Bingzi, he was demoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingzi, he was demoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 幽於和州，命控鶴軍使王宏將兵二百衛之。

translations.literal: He was confined at Hezhou, and Crane-Control Army Commissioner Wang Hong was ordered to lead two hundred troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: He was confined at Hezhou, and Wang Hong, commissioner of the Crane-Control Army, was ordered to lead two hundred troops to guard him.

sentences.zh: 劉昫與馮道婚姻。

translations.literal: Liu Xu and Feng Dao were connected by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu and Feng Dao were connected by marriage.

sentences.zh: 蚼性苛察，李愚剛褊；

translations.literal: Xu was by nature harsh and scrutinizing; Li Yu was stern and narrow-minded;
translations.idiomatic: Xu was by nature harsh and scrutinizing; Li Yu was stern and narrow-minded.

sentences.zh: 道既出鎮，二人論議多不合，事有應改者，愚謂昫曰：「此賢親家所為，更之不亦便乎！」

translations.literal: After Dao had gone out to his commission, the two men's deliberations often did not agree. When there were matters that ought to be changed, Yu said to Xu, "This was done by your worthy in-law—would it not be convenient to change it!"
translations.idiomatic: After Dao had gone out to his commission, the two men's deliberations often did not agree. When there were matters that ought to be changed, Yu said to Xu, "This was done by your worthy in-law—would it not be convenient to change it!"

sentences.zh: 昫恨之，由是動成忿爭，至相詬罵，各欲非時求見，事多凝滯。

translations.literal: Xu resented this, and from then on they constantly fell into angry disputes, even hurling abuse at each other. Each wished to seek audience at improper times, and affairs were often delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu resented this, and from then on they constantly fell into angry disputes, even hurling abuse at each other. Each wished to seek audience at improper times, and affairs were often delayed.

sentences.zh: 帝患之，欲更命相，問所親信以朝臣聞望宜為相者，皆以尚書左丞姚顗、太常卿盧文紀、秘書監崔居儉對；

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled by this and wished to appoint new chief councillors. He asked those he trusted which court officials of repute were suitable to be chief councillors, and all named Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Yao Yan, Grand Master of Ceremonies Lu Wenji, and Director of the Secretariat Library Cui Jujian;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was troubled by this and wished to appoint new chief councillors. He asked those he trusted which court officials of repute were suitable to be chief councillors, and all named Yao Yan, left assistant director of the secretariat; Lu Wenji, grand master of ceremonies; and Cui Jujian, director of the secretariat library.

sentences.zh: 論其才行，互有優劣。

translations.literal: When their conduct and ability were discussed, each had strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: When their conduct and ability were discussed, each had strengths and weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 帝不能決，乃置其名於琉璃瓶，夜焚香祝天，且以筋挾之，首得文紀，次得顗。

translations.literal: The emperor could not decide, so he placed their names in a glass jar, burned incense at night and prayed to Heaven, and drew them out with chopsticks. Wenji came out first, then Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not decide, so he placed their names in a glass jar, burned incense at night and prayed to Heaven, and drew them out with chopsticks. Wenji came out first, then Yan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛亥，以文紀為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Xinhai, Wenji was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Xinhai, Wenji was made vice director of the secretariat and co-grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 居儉，蕘之子也。

translations.literal: Jujian was the son of Rao.
translations.idiomatic: Jujian was the son of Cui Rao.

sentences.zh: 帝欲殺楚匡祚，韓昭胤曰：「陛下為天下父，天下之人皆陛下子，用法宜存至公，匡祚受詔檢校重吉家財，不得不爾。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to kill Chu Kuangzuo. Han Zhaoyin said, "Your Majesty is father to the realm, and all people under Heaven are Your Majesty's children. In applying the law one ought to preserve utmost fairness. Kuangzuo received an edict to inspect and take inventory of Chongji's family property and could not do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to kill Chu Kuangzuo. Han Zhaoyin said, "Your Majesty is father to the realm, and all people under Heaven are Your Majesty's children. In applying the law one ought to preserve utmost fairness. Kuangzuo received an edict to inspect and take inventory of Chongji's family property and could not do otherwise.

sentences.zh: 今族匡祚，無益死者，恐不厭眾心。」

translations.literal: To exterminate Kuangzuo's clan now would not benefit the dead and I fear would not satisfy popular sentiment."
translations.idiomatic: To exterminate Kuangzuo's clan now would not benefit the dead and I fear would not satisfy popular sentiment."

sentences.zh: 乙卯，長流匡祚於登州。

translations.literal: On the day Yimao, Kuangzuo was exiled far to Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yimao, Kuangzuo was exiled far to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，立沛國夫人劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On the day Dingsi, Lady Liu of Pei was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dingsi, Lady Liu of Pei was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 回鶻入貢者多為河西雜虜所掠，詔將軍牛知柔帥禁後衛送，與邠州兵共討之。

translations.literal: Many Uyghur tribute missions were plundered by various tribes of Hexi. An edict ordered General Niu Zhirou to lead the rear guard of the palace guard to escort them and, together with Binzhou troops, jointly campaign against the plunderers.
translations.idiomatic: Many Uyghur tribute missions were plundered by various tribes of Hexi. An edict ordered General Niu Zhirou to lead the rear guard of the palace guard to escort them and, together with Binzhou troops, jointly campaign against the plunderers.

sentences.zh: 吳徐知誥召右僕謝兼中書侍郎、同平章事宋齊丘還金陵，以為諸道都統判官，加司空，於事皆無所關預，齊丘屢請退居，知誥以南園給之。

translations.literal: In Wu, Xu Zhigao summoned Right Vice Director, concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councillor Song Qiqiu back to Jinling and made him chief staff officer of the overall command of all circuits, with the additional title Grand Master of Works. He had no part in any affairs, and Qiqiu repeatedly asked to retire from office. Zhigao granted him the Southern Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Xu Zhigao summoned Song Qiqiu, right vice director, concurrently vice director of the secretariat and co-grand councillor, back to Jinling and made him chief staff officer of the overall command of all circuits, with the additional title grand master of works. He had no part in any affairs, and Qiqiu repeatedly asked to retire from office. Zhigao granted him the Southern Garden.

sentences.zh: 護國節度使洋王從璋，歸德節度使涇王從敏，皆罷鎮居洛陽私第，帝待之甚薄；

translations.literal: Huguo Military Commissioner, Prince of Yang Congzhang, and Guide Military Commissioner, Prince of Jing Congmin were both removed from their commissions and lived in private residences at Luoyang. The emperor treated them very coldly;
translations.idiomatic: Congzhang, Prince of Yang, military commissioner of Huguo, and Congmin, Prince of Jing, military commissioner of Guide, were both removed from their commissions and lived in private residences at Luoyang. The emperor treated them very coldly.

sentences.zh: 從敏在宋州預殺重吉，帝尤惡之。

translations.literal: Congmin had taken part in killing Chongji at Songzhou, and the emperor especially hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Congmin had taken part in killing Chongji at Songzhou, and the emperor especially hated him.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴禁中，酒酣，顧二王曰：「爾等皆何物，輒據雄籓！」

translations.literal: Once, while attending a banquet in the palace, when the wine had gone to his head he turned to the two princes and said, "What sort of things are you, that you dare occupy mighty frontier commissions!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending a banquet in the palace, when the wine had gone to his head he turned to the two princes and said, "What sort of things are you, that you dare occupy mighty frontier commissions!"

sentences.zh: 二王大懼，太后叱之曰：「帝醉矣，爾曹速去！」

translations.literal: The two princes were greatly afraid. The empress dowager scolded him, saying, "The emperor is drunk—be off at once!"
translations.idiomatic: The two princes were greatly afraid. The empress dowager scolded him, saying, "The emperor is drunk—be off at once!"

sentences.zh: 蜀置永平軍於雅州，以孫漢韶為節度使。

translations.literal: Shu established the Yongping Army at Yazhou and made Sun Hanshao its military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shu established the Yongping Army at Yazhou and made Sun Hanshao its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 復以張虔釗為山南西道節度使、同平章事；

translations.literal: Zhang Qianzhao was again made Shannan West Circuit Military Commissioner and Co-Grand Councillor;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qianzhao was again made military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit and co-grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 虔釗固辭不行。

translations.literal: Qianzhao firmly declined and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhao firmly declined and would not go.

sentences.zh: 蜀主得風疾逾年，至是增劇。

translations.literal: The ruler of Shu had suffered from wind ailment for more than a year; at this time it grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Shu had suffered from wind ailment for more than a year; at this time it grew worse.

sentences.zh: 甲子，立子東川節度使、同平章事、親衛馬步都指揮使仁贊為太子，仍監國。

translations.literal: On the day Jiazi, his son Dongchuan Military Commissioner, Co-Grand Councillor, and Personal Guard horse-and-foot Commander-in-Chief Renzan was installed as crown prince and continued as regent of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiazi, his son Renzan, military commissioner of Dongchuan, co-grand councillor, and personal guard horse-and-foot commander-in-chief, was installed as crown prince and continued as regent of the realm.

sentences.zh: 召司空、同平章事趙季良、武信節度使李仁罕、保寧節度使趙廷隱、樞密使王處回、捧聖控鶴都指揮使張公鐸、奉鑾肅衛指揮副使侯弘實受遣詔輔政。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Works and Co-Grand Councillor Zhao Jiliang, Wuxin Military Commissioner Li Renhan, Baoning Military Commissioner Zhao Tingyin, Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Chuhui, Sacred-Bearer Crane-Control Commander-in-Chief Zhang Gongduo, and Ceremonial Escort and Strict Guard Deputy Commander Hou Hongshi were summoned to receive the deathbed edict and assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jiliang, grand master of works and co-grand councillor; Li Renhan, military commissioner of Wuxin; Zhao Tingyin, military commissioner of Baoning; Wang Chuhui, commissioner of military affairs; Zhang Gongduo, commander-in-chief of the Sacred-Bearer Crane-Control forces; and Hou Hongshi, deputy commander of the ceremonial escort and strict guard, were summoned to receive the deathbed edict and assist in governance.

sentences.zh: 是夕殂，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: That evening he died, and the death was kept secret without announcing mourning.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he died, and the death was kept secret without announcing mourning.

sentences.zh: 王處回夜啟義興門告趙季良，處回泣不已，季良正色曰：「今強將握兵，專伺時變，宜速立嗣君以絕覬覦，豈可但相泣邪！」

translations.literal: Wang Chuhui opened the Yixing Gate at night and told Zhao Jiliang. Chuhui wept without cease. Jiliang said with stern countenance, "Now powerful generals hold troops and watch only for the moment to change. You ought quickly to install the heir to cut off covetous eyes—how can you merely weep at each other!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chuhui opened the Yixing Gate at night and told Zhao Jiliang. Chuhui wept without cease. Jiliang said with stern countenance, "Now powerful generals hold troops and watch only for the moment to change. You ought quickly to install the heir to cut off covetous eyes—how can you merely weep at each other!"

sentences.zh: 處回收淚謝之。

translations.literal: Chuhui wiped away his tears and apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhui wiped away his tears and apologized to him.

sentences.zh: 季良教處回見李什罕，審其詞旨然後告之。

translations.literal: Jiliang instructed Chuhui to see Li Renhan, observe the tenor of his words, and only then tell him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiliang instructed Chuhui to see Li Renhan, observe the tenor of his words, and only then tell him.

sentences.zh: 處回至仁罕第，仁罕設備而出，遂不以實告。

translations.literal: Chuhui went to Renhan's residence. Renhan came out fully armed and on guard, so he was not told the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhui went to Renhan's residence. Renhan came out fully armed and on guard, so he was not told the truth.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，宣遺制，命太子仁贊更名昶，丁卯，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On the day Bingyin, the deathbed edict was proclaimed, ordering Crown Prince Renzan to change his name to Chang. On the day Dingmao he ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingyin, the deathbed edict was proclaimed, ordering Crown Prince Renzan to change his name to Chang. On the day Dingmao he ascended the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以王玫對左藏見財失實，故以劉昫代判三司。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Wang Mei's report on the visible wealth of the Left Treasury had not matched reality, the emperor had Liu Xu replace him in administering the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Wang Mei's report on the visible wealth of the Left Treasury had not matched reality, the emperor had Liu Xu replace him in administering the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 昫命判官高延賞鉤考窮核，皆積年逋欠之數，奸吏利其征責丐取，故存之。

translations.literal: Xu ordered administrative aide Gao Yanxiang to investigate exhaustively. All were figures of arrears accumulated over years; corrupt clerks profited from their collection and extortion and therefore kept them on the books.
translations.idiomatic: Xu ordered administrative aide Gao Yanxiang to investigate exhaustively. All were figures of arrears accumulated over years; corrupt clerks profited from their collection and extortion and therefore kept them on the books.

sentences.zh: 昫具奏其狀，且請察其可征者急督之，必無可償者悉蠲之，韓昭胤極言其便。

translations.literal: Xu fully memorialized the situation and also asked that among those that could be collected, collection be urgently pressed, while those that could certainly not be repaid be wholly remitted. Han Zhaoyin strongly argued the convenience of this.
translations.idiomatic: Xu fully memorialized the situation and also asked that among those that could be collected, collection be urgently pressed, while those that could certainly not be repaid be wholly remitted. Han Zhaoyin strongly argued the convenience of this.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚午，詔長興以前戶部及諸道逋租三百三十八萬，虛煩簿籍，鹹蠲免勿征。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day Gengwu, an edict ordered that the 3,380,000 in arrears owed to the Ministry of Revenue and the various circuits before the Changxing era be wholly remitted and not collected, since they needlessly vexed the ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day Gengwu, an edict declared that 3,380,000 in tax arrears owed to the Ministry of Revenue and the various circuits before the Changxing era would be remitted in full and no longer collected, on the grounds that they needlessly cluttered the registers.

sentences.zh: 貧民大悅，而三司吏怨之。

translations.literal: The poor rejoiced greatly, but the clerks of the Three Departments resented it.
translations.idiomatic: The poor rejoiced, but the clerks of the Three Departments resented the move.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以姚顗為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day Xinwei, Yao Yan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinwei, Yao Yan was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 右龍武統軍索自通，以河中之隙，心不自安，戊子，退朝過洛，自投於水而卒。

translations.literal: Suo Zitong, commander-in-chief of the Right Longwu Army, because of the breach over Hezhong could not feel secure in his heart. On the day Wuzi, after leaving court he passed the Luo River, threw himself into the water, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Zitong, commander-in-chief of the Right Longwu Army, felt insecure after the breach over Hezhong. On the day Wuzi, after leaving court he passed the Luo River, threw himself into the water, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之大驚，贈太尉。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he was greatly shocked and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly shocked when he heard of it and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以前安國節度使、同平章事趙鳳為太子太保。

translations.literal: On the day Bingshen, former Anguo Military Commissioner and Co-Grand Councillor Zhao Feng was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingshen, Zhao Feng, former military commissioner of Anguo and Co-Grand Councillor, was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸卯，詔鳳翔益兵守東安鎮以備蜀。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day Guimao, an edict ordered Fengxiang to increase troops to guard Dong'an Fort against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day Guimao, an edict ordered Fengxiang to reinforce Dong'an Fort with additional troops as a precaution against Shu.

sentences.zh: 蜀衛聖諸軍都指揮使、武信節度使李仁罕自恃宿將有功，復受顧托，求判六軍，令進奏吏宋從會以意諭樞密院，又至學士院偵草麻。

translations.literal: Li Renhan, overall commander of the Weisheng Armies and military commissioner of Wuxin, relying on his long service and merit and having again received the late ruler's trust, sought to administer the Six Armies. He had memorial clerk Song Conghui convey his intent to the Bureau of Military Affairs and also went to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies to spy on the drafting of the appointment edict.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renhan, overall commander of the Weisheng Armies and military commissioner of Wuxin, counted on his long service and past merit and on having again received the late ruler's trust, and sought command of the Six Armies. He had memorial clerk Song Conghui convey his wishes to the Bureau of Military Affairs and also went to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies to watch for the drafting of the appointment edict.

sentences.zh: 蜀主不得已，甲寅，加仁罕兼中書令，判六軍事；

translations.literal: The ruler of Shu had no choice. On the day Jiayin, Renhan was additionally made Concurrent Director of the Secretariat and was ordered to administer the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Shu had no choice. On the day Jiayin, Renhan was additionally appointed Concurrent Director of the Secretariat and put in charge of the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 以左匡聖都指揮使、保寧節度使趙廷隱兼侍中，為之副。

translations.literal: Zuo Kuangsheng overall commander and Baoning Military Commissioner Zhao Tingyin was made Concurrent Palace Attendant to serve as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingyin, overall commander of the Left Kuangsheng Army and military commissioner of Baoning, was made Concurrent Palace Attendant to serve as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 己未，雲州奏契丹入寇，北面招討使石敬瑭奏自將兵屯百井以備契丹。

translations.literal: On the day Jiwei, Yun Prefecture reported that the Khitans had invaded. Northern Campaign Commissioner Shi Jingtang memorialized that he would personally lead troops to encamp at Baijing to guard against the Khitans.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiwei, Yun Prefecture reported a Khitan incursion. Northern Campaign Commissioner Shi Jingtang memorialized that he would personally lead troops to encamp at Baijing against the Khitans.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，敬瑭奏振武節度使楊檀擊契丹於境上，卻之。

translations.literal: On the day Xinyou, Jingtang memorialized that Zhenwu Military Commissioner Yang Tan had struck the Khitans on the border and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinyou, Jingtang reported that Yang Tan, military commissioner of Zhenwu, had attacked the Khitans on the frontier and driven them back.

sentences.zh: 蜀奉鑾肅衛都指揮使、昭武節度使兼侍中李肇聞蜀主即位，顧望，不時入朝，至漢州，留與親戚燕飲逾旬；

translations.literal: Li Zhao, overall commander of the Fengluan Suwei Guard and military commissioner of Zhaowu and Concurrent Palace Attendant, on hearing that the ruler of Shu had ascended the throne hesitated and dallied and did not enter court at the proper time. Reaching Han Prefecture, he stayed there feasting with kinsmen for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao, overall commander of the Fengluan Suwei Guard and military commissioner of Zhaowu and Concurrent Palace Attendant, hesitated when he heard that the ruler of Shu had taken the throne and did not come to court promptly. At Han Prefecture he lingered for more than ten days, feasting with relatives.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚午，始至成都，稱足疾，扶杖入朝見，見蜀主不拜。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day Gengwu, he finally reached Chengdu. Claiming illness of the foot, he entered court leaning on a staff to be received, and when he saw the ruler of Shu he did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day Gengwu, he finally reached Chengdu. Claiming a foot ailment, he entered court leaning on a staff to be received, and when he saw the ruler of Shu he did not bow.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，左僕射、門下侍郎、同平章事李愚罷守本官，吏部尚書兼門下侍郎、同平章事、判三司劉昫罷為右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day Wuyin, Left Vice Director Li Yu was dismissed and retained his original office. Minister of Personnel and Concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Grand Councillor and Administrator of the Three Departments Liu Xu was dismissed and made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuyin, Li Yu, Left Vice Director, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Co-Grand Councillor, was dismissed and retained his original rank. Liu Xu, Minister of Personnel, Vice Director of the Chancellery, Co-Grand Councillor, and administrator of the Three Departments, was dismissed and made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 三司吏聞昫罷相，皆相駕，無一人從歸第者。

translations.literal: When the clerks of the Three Departments heard that Xu had been dismissed as chancellor, they all drove away together; not one followed him home.
translations.idiomatic: When the clerks of the Three Departments heard that Xu had lost the chancellorship, they all deserted him at once; not one followed him home.

sentences.zh: 蜀捧聖控鶴都指揮使張公鐸與醫官使韓繼勳、豐德庫使韓保貞、茶酒庫使安思謙等皆事蜀主於籓邸，素凶李仁罕，共譖之雲仁罕有異志；

translations.literal: Zhang Gongduo, overall commander of the Pingsheng Konghe Army, together with Medical Commissioner Han Jixun, Commissioner of the Fengde Storehouse Han Baozhen, Commissioner of the Tea and Wine Storehouse An Siqian, and others had all served the ruler of Shu in his princely residence. They had long hated Li Renhan and jointly slandered him, saying Renhan harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongduo, overall commander of the Pingsheng Konghe Army, together with Medical Commissioner Han Jixun, Commissioner of the Fengde Storehouse Han Baozhen, Commissioner of the Tea and Wine Storehouse An Siqian, and others had all served the ruler of Shu when he was still heir. They had long hated Li Renhan and jointly slandered him, claiming that Renhan harbored rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 蜀主令繼勳等與趙季良，趙廷隱謀，因仁罕入朝，命武士，執而殺之。

translations.literal: The ruler of Shu ordered Jixun and the others to plot with Zhao Jiliang and Zhao Tingyin. When Renhan entered court, armed warriors were commanded to seize and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Shu had Jixun and the others plot with Zhao Jiliang and Zhao Tingyin. When Renhan came to court, he ordered armed warriors to seize and kill him.

sentences.zh: 癸未，下詔暴其罪，並其子繼宏及宋從會等數人皆伏誅。

translations.literal: On the day Guiwei, an edict was issued exposing his crimes, and together with his son Jihong and Song Conghui and several others, all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guiwei, an edict exposed his crimes, and his son Jihong, Song Conghui, and several others were all executed.

sentences.zh: 是日，李肇釋杖而拜。

translations.literal: That same day, Li Zhao set aside his staff and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, Li Zhao set aside his staff and bowed.

sentences.zh: 蜀渠州都押牙文景琛據城叛，果州刺史李延厚討平之，蜀主左右以李肇倨慢，請誅之；

translations.literal: Wen Jingchen, chief military adjutant of Qu Prefecture in Shu, seized the city and rebelled. Guo Prefecture Commissioner Li Yanhou suppressed and pacified him. The ruler of Shu's attendants, because Li Zhao had been arrogant and disrespectful, asked that he be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jingchen, chief military adjutant of Qu Prefecture in Shu, seized the city and rebelled. Li Yanhou, commissioner of Guo Prefecture, suppressed the revolt. The ruler of Shu's attendants, citing Li Zhao's arrogance and disrespect, asked that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以肇為太子少傅致仕，徙邛州。

translations.literal: On the day Wuzi, Zhao was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office, and was transferred to Qiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuzi, Zhao was appointed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office, and was transferred to Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吳主加徐知誥大丞相、尚父、嗣齊王、九錫，辭不受。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu added to Xu Zhigao the titles Grand Chancellor, Venerable Father, Heir to the Prince of Qi, and the Nine Bestowals. He declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu offered Xu Zhigao the titles Grand Chancellor, Venerable Father, Heir to the Prince of Qi, and the Nine Bestowals. He declined them.

sentences.zh: 雄武節度使張延朗將兵圍文州，階州刺史郭知瓊拔尖石寨。

translations.literal: Xiongwu Military Commissioner Zhang Yanlang led troops to besiege Wen Prefecture. Jie Prefecture Commissioner Guo Zhiqiong captured Jianshi Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanlang, military commissioner of Xiongwu, led troops to besiege Wen Prefecture. Guo Zhiqiong, commissioner of Jie Prefecture, captured Jianshi Fort.

sentences.zh: 蜀李延厚將果州兵屯興州，遣先登指揮使范延暉將兵救文州，延朗解圍而歸。

translations.literal: In Shu, Li Yanhou led Guo Prefecture troops to encamp at Xing Prefecture and dispatched Vanguard Commander Fan Yanhui to lead troops to relieve Wen Prefecture. Yanlang lifted the siege and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu, Li Yanhou led troops from Guo Prefecture to encamp at Xing Prefecture and sent Vanguard Commander Fan Yanhui to relieve Wen Prefecture. Yanlang lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 興州刺史馮暉自乾渠引戍兵歸鳳翔。

translations.literal: Xing Prefecture Commissioner Feng Hui led garrison troops from Ganqu back to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui, commissioner of Xing Prefecture, led the garrison troops from Ganqu back to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，徐知誥召其子司徒、同平章事景通還金陵，為鎮海、寧國節度副大使、諸道副都統、判中外諸軍事；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Xu Zhigao summoned his son, Minister of Works and Co-Grand Councillor Jingtong, back to Jinling and made him Deputy Military Commissioner of Zhenhai and Ningguo, Deputy Overall Commander of the Various Circuits, and Administrator of All Internal and External Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Xu Zhigao summoned his son Jingtong, Minister of Works and Co-Grand Councillor, back to Jinling and appointed him Deputy Military Commissioner of Zhenhai and Ningguo, Deputy Overall Commander of the Various Circuits, and administrator of all internal and external military affairs.

sentences.zh: 以次子牙內馬步都指揮使、海州團練使景遷為左右軍都軍使、左僕射、參政事，留江都輔政。

translations.literal: His next son, Inner Guard Cavalry and Infantry Commander and Haidong Prefecture Training Commissioner Jingqian, was made Commander of the Left and Right Armies, Left Vice Director, and Participant in Governance, and was left at Jiangdu to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: His next son, Jingqian, Inner Guard Cavalry and Infantry Commander and training commissioner of Haizhou, was made Commander of the Left and Right Armies, Left Vice Director, and participant in governance, and was left at Jiangdu to assist in government.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己巳，以易州刺史安叔千為振武節度使，齊州防禦使尹暉為彰國節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day Jisi, Yi Prefecture Commissioner An Shuqian was made Zhenwu Military Commissioner, and Qi Prefecture Defense Commissioner Yin Hui was made Zhangguo Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day Jisi, An Shuqian, commissioner of Yi Prefecture, was appointed military commissioner of Zhenwu, and Yin Hui, defense commissioner of Qi Prefecture, was appointed military commissioner of Zhangguo.

sentences.zh: 叔千，沙陀人也。

translations.literal: Shuqian was a man of the Shatuo.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqian was a Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 壬申，石敬瑭奏契丹引去，罷兵歸。

translations.literal: On the day Renshen, Shi Jingtang memorialized that the Khitans had withdrawn and that the troops were dismissed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renshen, Shi Jingtang reported that the Khitans had withdrawn and that he was dismissing the troops and returning.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，征雄武節度使張延朗為中書侍郎、同平章事、判三司。

translations.literal: On the day Yihai, Xiongwu Military Commissioner Zhang Yanlang was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Secretariat, Co-Grand Councillor, and Administrator of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yihai, Zhang Yanlang, military commissioner of Xiongwu, was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Secretariat, Co-Grand Councillor, and administrator of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，漢皇后馬氏殂。

translations.literal: On the day Xinsi, Empress Ma of Han died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinsi, Empress Ma of Han died.

sentences.zh: 甲申，蜀葬文武聖德英烈明孝皇帝於和陵，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: On the day Jiashen, Shu buried the Emperor of Civil and Military Sagely Virtue, Heroic Brilliance, and Bright Filial Piety at Heling Mausoleum, with the temple name Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiashen, Shu buried the Emperor of Civil and Military Sagely Virtue, Heroic Brilliance, and Bright Filial Piety at Heling Mausoleum, with the temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，葬鄂王於徽陵城南，封才數尺；

translations.literal: On the day Yiyou, the Prince of E was buried south of Huiling Mausoleum; the mound was only a few feet high.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yiyou, the Prince of E was buried south of Huiling Mausoleum; the mound rose only a few feet.

sentences.zh: 觀者悲之。

translations.literal: Those who looked on were grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers were moved to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 是歲秋、冬旱，民多流亡，同、華、蒲、絳尤甚。

translations.literal: That year drought continued through autumn and winter, and many of the people fled. Tong, Hua, Pu, and Jiang were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: That year drought persisted through autumn and winter, and many people fled their homes. The suffering was especially severe in Tong, Hua, Pu, and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 漢主命判六軍秦王弘度募宿衛兵千人，皆市井無賴子弟，弘度暱之。

translations.literal: The ruler of Han ordered Prince of Qin Hongdu, who administered the Six Armies, to recruit a thousand palace-guard soldiers, all idle youths of the marketplace. Hongdu grew close to them.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Han ordered Prince of Qin Hongdu, administrator of the Six Armies, to recruit a thousand palace-guard soldiers from the riffraff of the marketplace. Hongdu grew fond of them.

sentences.zh: 同平章事楊洞潛諫曰：「秦王，國之塚嫡，宜親端士。

translations.literal: Co-Grand Councillor Yang Dongqian remonstrated, saying, "The Prince of Qin is the direct heir of the state. He ought to keep company with upright gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Co-Grand Councillor Yang Dongqian remonstrated, saying, "The Prince of Qin is the direct heir of the realm. He ought to keep company with upright gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 使之治軍已過矣，況暱群小乎！」

translations.literal: To have him administer troops is already going too far—how much more to be intimate with petty men!"
translations.idiomatic: Putting him in charge of troops is already going too far—how much worse to grow close to petty men!"

sentences.zh: 漢主曰：「小兒教以戎事，過煩公憂。」

translations.literal: The ruler of Han said, "I am teaching the boy military affairs. You worry too much."
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Han said, "I am merely teaching the boy military affairs. You need not worry so much."

sentences.zh: 終不戒弘度。

translations.literal: In the end he did not warn Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not restrain Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 洞潛出，見衛士掠商人金帛，商人不敢訴，漢曰：「政亂如此，安用宰相！」

translations.literal: Dongqian went out and saw guards seizing merchants' gold and silk. The merchants dared not complain. Dongqian said, "When government is this chaotic, what use is there in a chancellor!"
translations.idiomatic: Dongqian went out and saw guards seizing merchants' gold and silk while the merchants dared not complain. He said, "When government is this chaotic, what use is there in a chancellor!"

sentences.zh: 因謝病歸第；

translations.literal: Thereupon he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，不召，遂卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he was not summoned, and he finally died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time without being summoned, he finally died.

sentences.zh: 潞王下清泰二年（

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Lu, the second year of Qingtai (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Lu, the second year of Qingtai (

sentences.zh: 乙未，公元九三五年）

translations.literal: Yiwei, AD 935)
translations.idiomatic: Yiwei, AD 935)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙申朔，閩大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day of the month Bingshen, Min proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the first day Bingshen, Min proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 改元永和。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was changed to Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙寅朔，蜀大赦。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day of the month Bingyin, Shu proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day Bingyin, Shu proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以樞密使、天雄節度使兼侍中范延光為宣武節度使兼中書令。

translations.literal: On the day Jiaxu, Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner and Tianxiong Military Commissioner and Concurrent Palace Attendant Fan Yanguang was made Xuannwu Military Commissioner and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiaxu, Fan Yanguang, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military commissioner of Tianxiong and Concurrent Palace Attendant, was appointed military commissioner of Xuannwu and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，夏州節度使李彝超上言疾病，以兄行軍司馬彝殷權知軍州事；

translations.literal: On the day Dingchou, Xia Prefecture Military Commissioner Li Yichao reported illness and had his elder brother, campaigning army vice marshal Yi Yin, provisionally administer military and prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dingchou, Li Yichao, military commissioner of Xia Prefecture, reported illness and had his elder brother Yi Yin, campaigning army vice marshal, provisionally administer military and prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 彝超尋卒。

translations.literal: Yichao soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Yichao soon died.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，蜀主尊母李氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: On the day Wuyin, the ruler of Shu honored his mother, Lady Li, as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuyin, the ruler of Shu honored his mother, Lady Li, as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后，太原人，本莊宗後宮也，以賜蜀高祖。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was a native of Taiyuan and had originally been in the rear palace of Zhuangzong. She was given to the Gaozu of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was from Taiyuan and had originally been a consort in Zhuangzong's rear palace before being given to the Gaozu of Shu.

sentences.zh: 己丑，追尊帝母魯國夫人魏氏曰宣憲皇太后。

translations.literal: On the day Jichou, the emperor's mother, Lady Wei of Lu, was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Xuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jichou, the emperor's mother, Lady Wei of Lu, was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Xuanxian.

sentences.zh: 閩主立淑妃陳氏為皇后。

translations.literal: The ruler of Min established Pure Consort Chen as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Min made Pure Consort Chen empress.

sentences.zh: 初，閩主兩娶劉氏，皆士族，美而無寵。

translations.literal: Earlier, the ruler of Min had twice married women of the Liu clan, both from gentry families, beautiful yet without favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the ruler of Min had twice married women of the Liu clan, both from distinguished families—beautiful, yet never favored.

sentences.zh: 陳后，本閩太祖侍婢金鳳也，陋而淫，閩主嬖之，以其族人守恩、匡勝為殿使。

translations.literal: Empress Chen had originally been Jinfeng, a serving maid of the Taizu of Min. She was plain and licentious, yet the ruler of Min doted on her and made her kinsmen Shou'en and Kuangsheng palace commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chen had originally been Jinfeng, a serving maid of the Taizu of Min. Plain and licentious, she nevertheless won the ruler of Min's favor, and he made her kinsmen Shou'en and Kuangsheng palace commissioners.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛丑，以前宣武節度使兼侍中趙延壽為忠武節度使兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day Xinmao, former Xuannwu Military Commissioner and Concurrent Palace Attendant Zhao Yanshou was made Zhongwu Military Commissioner and Concurrent Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day Xinmao, Zhao Yanshou, former military commissioner of Xuannwu and Concurrent Palace Attendant, was appointed military commissioner of Zhongwu and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以李彝殷為定難節度使。

translations.literal: Li Yiyin was made Dingnan Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yiyin was appointed military commissioner of Dingnan.

sentences.zh: 己酉，贈吳越王元瓘母陳氏為晉國太夫人。

translations.literal: On the day Jiyou, the mother of Wuyue King Yuangui, Lady Chen, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiyou, Lady Chen, mother of Wuyue King Yuangui, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Jin.

sentences.zh: 元瓘性孝，尊禮母黨，厚加賜與，而未嘗遷官，授以重任。

translations.literal: Yuangui was filial by nature. He honored and treated his mother's kin with ceremony and gave them generous rewards, yet he never promoted them to office or entrusted them with weighty duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui was filial by nature. He honored his mother's kin and rewarded them generously, yet he never promoted them to office or entrusted them with important duties.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以彰聖都指揮使安審琦領順化節度使。

translations.literal: On the day Renxu, Zhangsheng overall commander An Shenqi was put in charge as Shunhua Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renxu, An Shenqi, overall commander of the Zhangsheng Army, was appointed military commissioner of Shunhua.

sentences.zh: 審琦，金全之子也。

translations.literal: Shenqi was the son of An Jinquan.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi was the son of An Jinquan.

sentences.zh: 太常丞史在德，性狂狷，上書歷詆內外文武之士，請遍加考試，黜陟能否。

translations.literal: Shi Zaide, assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was wild and obstinate by nature. He submitted a memorial slandering one after another the civil and military officials within and without, and asked that examinations be applied universally to demote or promote according to ability.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zaide, assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was wild and obstinate by nature. He submitted a memorial denouncing civil and military officials throughout the court and asked that universal examinations be held to promote or demote them according to merit.

sentences.zh: 執政及朝士大怒，盧文紀及補闕劉濤、楊昭儉等皆請加罪。

translations.literal: Those in power and the court officials were greatly angered. Lu Wenji and remonstrance officials Liu Tao, Yang Zhaojian, and others all asked that punishment be added.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power and the court officials were furious. Lu Wenji and remonstrance officials Liu Tao, Yang Zhaojian, and others all asked that he be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝謂學士馬胤孫曰：「朕新臨天下，宜開言路；

translations.literal: The emperor said to Academician Ma Yinsun, "I have newly come to rule the realm and ought to open the path of speech.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Academician Ma Yinsun, "I have only just come to rule the realm and ought to keep the path of speech open.

sentences.zh: 若朝士以言獲罪，誰敢言者！

translations.literal: If court officials are punished for speaking, who will dare speak!
translations.idiomatic: If court officials are punished for speaking out, who will dare speak!

sentences.zh: 卿為朕作詔書，宣朕意。」

translations.literal: You compose an edict for me and proclaim my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Draft an edict for me and proclaim my intent."

sentences.zh: 乃下詔，略曰：「昔魏徵請賞皇甫德參，今濤等請黜史在德；

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued, saying in summary, "Formerly Wei Zheng asked that Huangfu Dekan be rewarded; now Tao and the others ask that Shi Zaide be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict was issued, saying in summary, "Formerly Wei Zheng asked that Huangfu Dekan be rewarded; now Tao and the others ask that Shi Zaide be demoted.

sentences.zh: 事同言異，何其遠哉！

translations.literal: The matter is the same yet the words differ—how far apart they are!
translations.idiomatic: The matter is the same, yet the words differ—how far apart they are!

sentences.zh: 在德情在傾輸，安可責也！」

translations.literal: Zaide's feelings lay in pouring himself out fully—how can he be blamed!"
translations.idiomatic: Zaide spoke from wholehearted devotion—how can he be blamed!"

sentences.zh: 昭儉，嗣復之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zhaojian was the great-grandson of Sifu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojian was the great-grandson of Sifu.

sentences.zh: 吳加徐景遷同平章事、知左右軍事；

translations.literal: Wu added to Xu Jingqian the titles Co-Grand Councillor and Administrator of the Left and Right Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Wu added to Xu Jingqian the titles Co-Grand Councillor and administrator of the Left and Right Armies.

sentences.zh: 徐知誥令尚書郎陳覺輔之，謂覺曰：「吾少時與宋子嵩論議，好相詰難，或吾捨子嵩還家，或子嵩拂衣而起。

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao ordered Secretariat Director Chen Jue to assist him and said to Jue, "When I was young I debated with Song Zisong and loved to cross-examine each other. Sometimes I would leave Zisong and go home, and sometimes Zisong would rise and depart in a huff.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao had Secretariat Director Chen Jue assist him and said to Jue, "When I was young I debated with Song Zisong and loved to cross-examine each other. Sometimes I would leave Zisong and go home; sometimes Zisong would rise and storm off.

sentences.zh: 子嵩攜衣笥望秦淮門欲去者數矣，吾常戒門者止之。

translations.literal: Zisong several times took up his clothes chest and looked toward the Qinhuai Gate intending to leave, and I always ordered the gatekeepers to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Several times Zisong took up his clothes chest and looked toward the Qinhuai Gate as if to leave, and I always ordered the gatekeepers to stop him.

sentences.zh: 吾今老矣，猶未遍達時事，況景遷年少當國，故屈吾子以誨之耳。」

translations.literal: I am old now and still have not fully mastered the affairs of the times—how much more so Jingqian, who is young and holds the realm. Therefore I have humbled myself to ask you, sir, to instruct him."
translations.idiomatic: I am old now and still have not fully mastered the affairs of the day—how much less can Jingqian, who is young and holds the realm. That is why I have asked you, sir, to guide him."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚午，蜀以御史中丞龍門毋昭裔為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day Gengwu, Shu made Censor-in-Chief Wu Zhaoyi of Longmen Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day Gengwu, Shu appointed Wu Zhaoyi of Longmen, Censor-in-Chief, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 癸未，加樞密使、刑部尚書韓昭胤中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day Guiwei, Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner and Minister of Justice Han Zhaoyin was additionally made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guiwei, Han Zhaoyin, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Minister of Justice, was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 辛卯。

translations.literal: On the day Xinmao.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinmao.

sentences.zh: 以宣徽南院使劉延皓為刑部尚書，充樞密使。

translations.literal: Southern Bureau Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Liu Yanhao was made Minister of Justice and appointed Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanhao, Southern Bureau Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed Minister of Justice and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 延皓，皇后之弟也。

translations.literal: Yanhao was the empress's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhao was the empress's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以左領軍衛大將軍劉延朗為本衛上將軍，充宣徽北院使，兼樞密副使。

translations.literal: On the day Guisi, Left Leading Army Guard General Liu Yanlang was made Senior General of that guard, appointed Northern Bureau Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, and made Deputy Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guisi, Liu Yanlang, general of the Left Leading Army Guard, was made senior general of that guard, appointed Northern Bureau Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, and made deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙申，契丹寇新州及振武。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day Bingshen, the Khitans raided Xin Prefecture and Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day Bingshen, the Khitans raided Xin Prefecture and Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，賜振武節度使楊檀名光遠。

translations.literal: On the day Gengxu, Zhenwu Military Commissioner Yang Tan was granted the name Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengxu, Yang Tan, military commissioner of Zhenwu, was granted the name Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 六月，吳德勝節度使兼中書令柴再用卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Desheng Military Commissioner and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat Chai Zaiyong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Chai Zaiyong, military commissioner of Desheng and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, died.

sentences.zh: 先是，史官王振嘗詢其戰功，再用曰：「鷹犬微效，皆社稷之靈，再用何功之有！」

translations.literal: Earlier, historiographer Wang Zhen had once inquired about his battle achievements. Zaiyong said, "Hawks and hounds render slight service—all is the numinous blessing of the altars of soil and grain. What achievement has Zaiyong!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, historiographer Wang Zhen had once asked about his battle achievements. Zaiyong said, "Hawks and hounds render slight service—all is the blessing of the state. What achievement have I!"

sentences.zh: 竟不報。

translations.literal: In the end he made no report.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he made no report.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇應州。

translations.literal: The Khitans raided Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans raided Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使、北面總管石敬瑭既還鎮，陰為自全之計。

translations.literal: Hedong Military Commissioner and Northern Overall Commander Shi Jingtang, having returned to his commission, secretly made plans for his own preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang, military commissioner of Hedong and Northern Overall Commander, having returned to his post, secretly made plans to preserve himself.

sentences.zh: 帝好咨訪外事，常命端明殿學士李專美、翰林學士李崧、知制誥呂琦、薛文遇、翰林天文趙延乂等更直於中興殿庭，與語或至夜分。

translations.literal: The emperor liked to consult on external affairs and often ordered Duanming Hall Academician Li Zhuanmei, Hanlin Academician Li Song, Drafting Edict Officials Lu Qi and Xue Wenyü, and Hanlin Astronomer Zhao Yanyi and others to rotate night duty in the courtyard of the Zhongxing Hall, speaking with them sometimes until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor liked to consult on external affairs and often had Duanming Hall Academician Li Zhuanmei, Hanlin Academician Li Song, drafting edict officials Lu Qi and Xue Wenyü, and Hanlin astronomer Zhao Yanyi and others rotate night duty in the courtyard of the Zhongxing Hall, talking with them sometimes until midnight.

sentences.zh: 時敬瑭二子為內使，曹太后則晉國長公主之母也。

translations.literal: At that time Jingtang's two sons served as inner envoys, and Empress Dowager Cao was the mother of the Jin Kingdom's eldest princess.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jingtang's two sons served as inner envoys, and Empress Dowager Cao was the mother of the eldest princess of Jin.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭賂太后左右，令伺帝之密謀，事無鉅細皆知之。

translations.literal: Jingtang bribed those around the empress dowager and had them spy on the emperor's secret plans. Matters great and small were all known to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang bribed those around the empress dowager and had them spy on the emperor's secret plans, so that he learned of matters great and small.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭多於賓客前自稱贏瘠不堪為帥，冀朝廷不之忌。

translations.literal: Jingtang often declared before guests that he was emaciated and unfit to serve as commander, hoping the court would not be wary of him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang often told guests that he was emaciated and unfit to serve as commander, hoping the court would not regard him as a threat.

sentences.zh: 時契丹屢寇北邊，禁軍多在幽、并，敬瑭與趙德鈞求益兵運糧，朝夕相繼。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitans repeatedly raided the northern border, and the imperial armies were mostly in You and Bing. Jingtang and Zhao Dejun sought increased troops and transport of grain, one memorial following another morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Khitans repeatedly raided the northern frontier, and the imperial armies were mostly stationed in You and Bing. Jingtang and Zhao Dejun petitioned incessantly for more troops and grain transport.

sentences.zh: 甲申，詔借河東人有蓄積者菽粟。

translations.literal: On the day Jiashen, an edict ordered that grain be borrowed from those in Hedong who had stores.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiashen, an edict ordered grain to be borrowed from those in Hedong who had stores.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔鎮州輸絹五萬匹於總管府，糴軍糧，率鎮冀人車千五百乘運糧於代州；

translations.literal: On the day Yiyou, an edict ordered Zhen Prefecture to deliver fifty thousand bolts of silk to the overall commander's headquarters to purchase army grain, and to lead fifteen hundred carts of men from Zhen and Ji to transport grain to Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yiyou, an edict ordered Zhen Prefecture to deliver fifty thousand bolts of silk to the overall commander's headquarters to purchase army grain, and to lead fifteen hundred carts from Zhen and Ji to transport grain to Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又詔魏博市糴。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Weibo to purchase grain.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered Weibo to purchase grain.

sentences.zh: 時水旱民饑，敬瑭遣使督趣嚴急，山東之民流散，亂始兆矣。

translations.literal: At that time [there were] floods and droughts [and] the people suffered famine. Jingtang sent envoys to supervise and press [for payment] with extreme severity. The people of Shandong scattered in flight, and the first signs of chaos appeared.
translations.idiomatic: At that time flood and drought left the people starving. Shi Jingtang sent agents to press for payments with brutal urgency. The common folk of Shandong fled their homes, and the first stirrings of rebellion began.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭將大軍屯忻州，朝廷遣使賜軍士夏衣，傳詔撫諭，軍士呼萬歲者數四。

translations.literal: Jingtang stationed a great army at Xin Prefecture. The court sent envoys to bestow summer garments on the soldiers, conveying an edict to comfort and instruct them. The soldiers shouted "Long live [the emperor]!" four times.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang camped a large force at Xinzhou. The court dispatched envoys with summer uniforms and an edict of reassurance for the troops. The soldiers cried "Long live the emperor!" four times over.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭懼，幕僚河內段希堯請誅其唱首者，敬瑭命都押衙劉知遠斬挾馬都將李暉等三十六人以徇。

translations.literal: Jingtang was afraid. His staff member Duan Xiyao of Henei asked to execute the ringleaders. Jingtang ordered the chief military inspector Liu Zhiyuan to behead Li Hui and thirty-five others, mounted adjutants, as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened by this display, Shi Jingtang's aide Duan Xiyao of Henei urged him to kill the ringleaders. Jingtang ordered Liu Zhiyuan, chief military inspector, to execute Li Hui and thirty-five other mounted adjutants as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 希堯，懷州人也。

translations.literal: Xiyao was a native of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyao was a native of Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，益疑敬瑭。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and grew even more suspicious of Jingtang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, his suspicions of Shi Jingtang only deepened.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔：「竊盜不計贓多少，並縱火強盜，並行極法。」

translations.literal: On the day Renchen, an edict [said]: "Petty theft, regardless of the amount of stolen goods, and arson and armed robbery alike shall all be punished by the extreme penalty."
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day, an edict was issued: "Petty theft, regardless of the value stolen, and arson and armed robbery alike shall all be punished by the utmost penalty."

sentences.zh: 閩福王繼鵬私於宮人李春燕，繼鵬請之於陳后，後白閩主而賜之。

translations.literal: Jipeng, Prince of Fu of Min, had a private affair with the palace woman Li Chunyan. Jipeng requested her from Empress Chen; the empress informed the ruler of Min, and he bestowed her [on Jipeng].
translations.idiomatic: Jipeng, Prince of Fu in Min, took the palace woman Li Chunyan as his lover. He asked Empress Chen for her; she told the ruler of Min, and he granted her to Jipeng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以樞密使劉延皓為天雄節度使。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Privy Council Commissioner Liu Yanhao was appointed Military Commissioner of Tianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Privy Council Commissioner Liu Yanhao was appointed military commissioner of Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以武寧節度使張敬達為北面行營副總管，將兵屯代州，以分石敬瑭之權。

translations.literal: On the day Yisi, Wuning Military Commissioner Zhang Jingda was appointed Deputy Overall Commander of the Northern Field Headquarters and led troops to camp at Dai Prefecture, in order to divide Shi Jingtang's authority.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day, Zhang Jingda, military commissioner of Wuning, was named deputy overall commander of the northern field headquarters and led troops to camp at Daizhou, dividing Shi Jingtang's authority.

sentences.zh: 帝深以時事為憂，嘗從容讓盧文紀等以無所規贊。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply worried about current affairs and once, in an easy manner, reproached Lu Wenji and the others for offering no counsel or support.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply troubled by affairs of state and once gently reproached Lu Wenji and his colleagues for offering no counsel.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，文紀等上言：「臣等每五日起居，與兩班旅見，暫獲對揚，侍衛滿前，雖有愚慮，不敢敷陳。

translations.literal: On the day Dingsi, Wenji and the others submitted a memorial: "We attend the five-day audience, appearing with the two ranks in procession. We briefly receive imperial response, with guards filling the space before us. Though we have humble thoughts, we dare not set them forth.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day, Wenji and the others memorialized the throne: "We attend the five-day audience and appear with the two ranks in procession. We are granted only a brief exchange, with guards crowding the hall before us. Though we have counsel to offer, we dare not speak freely.

sentences.zh: 竊見前朝自上元以來，置延英殿，或宰相欲有奏論，天子欲有咨度，皆非時召對，旁無侍衛，故人得盡言。

translations.literal: We have observed that from the Shangyuan reign of the former dynasty onward, the Yanying Hall was established. When a chief minister wished to submit a discussion, or the Son of Heaven wished to consult, both were summoned for audience at irregular times, with no attendants at the side, so that people could speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: We note that since the Shangyuan reign of the previous dynasty, the Yanying Hall was established so that when a chief minister wished to discuss policy, or the emperor wished to consult, they could be summoned at any time without attendants present, and speak freely.

sentences.zh: 望復此故事，惟聽機要之臣侍側。」

translations.literal: We hope to restore this old practice, allowing only confidential ministers to attend at the side."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that this old practice be restored, with only trusted ministers in attendance."

sentences.zh: 詔以「舊制五日起居，百僚俱退，宰相獨升，若常事自可敷奏。

translations.literal: An edict [replied]: "Under the old system of the five-day audience, all officials withdraw and the chief ministers alone ascend. If the matter is routine, one may naturally set it forth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Under the old system of the five-day audience, all officials withdraw and the chief ministers alone remain. Routine matters may naturally be submitted then.

sentences.zh: 或事應嚴密，不以其日，或異日聽於閣門奏榜子，當盡屏侍臣，於便殿相待，何必襲延英之名也！」

translations.literal: If a matter should be kept strictly confidential, it need not be on that day; on another day one may be heard at the Gatehouse submitting a memorial slip. Attendants should all be dismissed, and one should meet in a convenient hall—why must one follow the name of Yanying!"
translations.idiomatic: If a matter requires strict confidentiality, it need not wait for that day; on another day you may submit a memorial slip at the Gatehouse. Attendants should be dismissed and you should meet in a private hall. Why must we revive the name Yanying?"

sentences.zh: 吳潤州團練使徐知諤，狎暱小人，游燕廢務，作列肆於牙城西，躬自貿易。

translations.literal: Xu Zhiyu, regimental training commissioner of Run Prefecture in Wu, was intimate with petty men, indulged in pleasure and neglected duties, set up a row of shops west of the yamen gate, and personally engaged in trade.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhiyu, regimental training commissioner of Runzhou in Wu, consorted with petty men, neglected his duties for pleasure, set up a row of shops west of the yamen gate, and traded there himself.

sentences.zh: 徐知誥聞之怒，召知諤左右詰責；

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao heard of it and was angry. He summoned Zhiyu's attendants and interrogated and rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Zhigao heard of this, he was furious and summoned Zhiyu's attendants for questioning and rebuke.

sentences.zh: 知諤懼。

translations.literal: Zhiyu was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu was terrified.

sentences.zh: 或謂知誥曰：「忠武王最愛知諤，而以後事傳於公。

translations.literal: Someone said to Zhigao: "Prince Zhongwu loved Zhiyu most, yet he passed the succession to you.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Zhigao, "Prince Zhongwu loved Zhiyu best, yet he passed the succession to you.

sentences.zh: 往年知詢失守，論議至今未息。

translations.literal: In former years Zhixun lost his post, and criticism has not ceased to this day.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixun lost his command in years past, the talk never fully died down.

sentences.zh: 借使知諤治有能名，訓兵養民，於公何利？」

translations.literal: Even if Zhiyu governed with a reputation for ability, trained troops and nourished the people—what advantage would that be to you?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if Zhiyu governed well, trained troops, and cared for the people, what would that gain you?"

sentences.zh: 知誥感悟，待之加厚。

translations.literal: Zhigao was moved to understanding and treated him with even greater favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao took the point and treated Zhiyu with even greater favor.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙申，吳大赦，改元天祚。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day Bingshen, Wu proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Tianzuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the bingshen day, Wu proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Tianzuo.

sentences.zh: 己酉，已宣徽南院使房暠為刑部尚書，充樞密使；

translations.literal: On the day Jiyou, Fang Gao, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was already [appointed] Minister of Justice and filled the post of Privy Council Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day, Fang Gao, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed Minister of Justice and privy council commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宣徽北院使劉延朗為南院使，仍兼樞密副使。

translations.literal: Liu Yanlang, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, became commissioner of the Southern Bureau and concurrently served as Deputy Privy Council Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanlang, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, became commissioner of the Southern Bureau and also served as deputy privy council commissioner.

sentences.zh: 於是延朗及樞密直學士薛文遇等居中用事，暠與趙延壽雖為使長，其聽用之言什不三四。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yanlang and Privy Council Direct Academician Xue Wenyü and others held power at court. Though Gao and Zhao Yanshou were the senior commissioners, only three or four tenths of what they said was heeded and adopted.
