translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Yanlang and Privy Council Direct Academician Xue Wenyü and others held real power at court. Though Gao and Zhao Yanshou were the senior commissioners, scarcely three or four words in ten that they spoke were heeded.

sentences.zh: 暠隨勢可否，不為事先；

translations.literal: Gao assented or denied according to the trend and did not take the lead in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao simply went along with whatever was prevailing and never took the initiative.

sentences.zh: 每幽、并遣使入奏，樞密諸人環坐議之，暠多俯首而寐，比覺，引頸振衣，則使者去矣。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys from You and Bing came to report, the privy council officials sat in a circle to discuss it. Gao mostly bowed his head and slept. By the time he awoke, stretched his neck, and shook out his robes, the envoys were already gone.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys from You and Bing arrived to report, the privy council officials would sit in a circle to discuss the matter. Gao usually bowed his head and dozed off. By the time he woke, stretched his neck, and shook out his robes, the envoys were already gone.

sentences.zh: 啟奏除授，一歸延朗。

translations.literal: Memorials, appointments, and dismissals all fell to Yanlang alone.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials and appointments alike were entirely Yanlang's to decide.

sentences.zh: 諸方鎮、刺史自外入者，必先賂延朗，後議貢獻。

translations.literal: Military commissioners and prefects coming in from the provinces had first to bribe Yanlang, and only afterward discuss tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioners and prefects arriving from the provinces had first to bribe Yanlang before tribute was even discussed.

sentences.zh: 賂厚者先，得內地；

translations.literal: Those who bribed heavily came first and received interior posts.
translations.idiomatic: Those who paid generously were served first and received posts in the interior.

sentences.zh: 賂薄者晚，得邊陲。

translations.literal: Those who bribed lightly came late and received frontier posts.
translations.idiomatic: Those who paid poorly waited longer and were sent to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 由是諸將帥皆怨憤，帝不能察。

translations.literal: Because of this all the generals and commanders resented and were indignant, but the emperor could not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the generals seethed with resentment, but the emperor remained unaware.

sentences.zh: 蜀金州防禦使全師郁寇金州，拔水寨。

translations.literal: Quan Shiyu, defense commissioner of Jin Prefecture in Shu, raided Jin Prefecture and captured the water fort.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Shiyu, defense commissioner of Jinzhou in Shu, attacked Jinzhou and captured its water fort.

sentences.zh: 城中兵才千人，都監陳知隱托它事將兵三百沿流遁去。

translations.literal: The troops in the city numbered only a thousand. Supervisory commander Chen Zhiyin, on the pretext of other business, led three hundred soldiers along the river and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The city held only a thousand troops. Supervisory commander Chen Zhiyin, on some pretext, led three hundred men downriver and fled.

sentences.zh: 防禦使馬全節罄私財以給軍，出奇死戰，蜀兵乃退。

translations.literal: Defense Commissioner Ma Quanjie exhausted his private wealth to supply the army, fought a desperate battle by surprise tactics, and the Shu troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Defense Commissioner Ma Quanjie spent his private fortune to supply the army, fought a desperate surprise battle, and drove the Shu troops back.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔斬知隱。

translations.literal: On the day Wuyin, an edict ordered Zhiyin beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day, an edict ordered Chen Zhiyin executed.

sentences.zh: 初，閩主有幸臣曰歸守明，出入臥內。

translations.literal: Earlier, the ruler of Min had a favored minister named Gui Shouming, who entered and left the sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the ruler of Min had a favored minister named Gui Shouming who came and went freely in the inner chambers.

sentences.zh: 閩主晚年得風疾，陳后與守明及百工院使李可殷私通，國人皆惡之，莫敢言。

translations.literal: In his later years the ruler of Min contracted a wind ailment. Empress Chen had a private liaison with Shouming and Li Keyin, commissioner of the Bureau of Artisans; the people of the state all hated this, but none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the ruler of Min was stricken with paralysis. Empress Chen carried on an affair with Shouming and Li Keyin, commissioner of the Bureau of Artisans. The people loathed this, but none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 可殷嘗譖皇城使李倣於閩主，后族陳匡勝無禮於福王繼鵬，倣及繼鵬皆恨之。

translations.literal: Keyin once slandered Li Fang, commissioner of the Imperial City, to the ruler of Min. Empress Chen's clansman Chen Kuangsheng was disrespectful toward Prince of Fu Jipeng. Fang and Jipeng both hated them.
translations.idiomatic: Keyin once slandered Li Fang, commissioner of the Imperial City, to the ruler of Min. Empress Chen's kinsman Chen Kuangsheng had insulted Prince Jipeng of Fu. Fang and Jipeng both hated them.

sentences.zh: 閩主疾甚，繼鵬有喜色。

translations.literal: When the ruler of Min's illness was severe, Jipeng showed a look of joy.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler of Min fell gravely ill, Jipeng could not hide his delight.

sentences.zh: 倣以閩主為必不起，冬，十月，己卯，使壯士數人持白梃擊李可殷，殺之，中外震驚。

translations.literal: Fang believed the ruler of Min would certainly not recover. In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Jimao, he sent several strong men bearing white clubs to strike Li Keyin and kill him. Within and without the court were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Fang believed the ruler of Min would not recover. In the tenth month of winter, on the jimao day, he sent several strong men with white clubs to beat Li Keyin to death. The court and the realm were stunned.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，閩主疾少間，陳后訴之。

translations.literal: On the day Gengchen, the ruler of Min's illness eased slightly, and Empress Chen complained to him.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day the ruler of Min briefly rallied, and Empress Chen lodged her complaint.

sentences.zh: 閩主力疾視朝，詰可殷死狀，倣懼而出，俄頃，引部兵鼓噪入宮。

translations.literal: The ruler of Min, forcing himself despite illness, held court and questioned the circumstances of Keyin's death. Fang fled in fear. In a moment he led his troops, shouting and clamoring, into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Min, forcing himself despite his illness, held court and demanded an account of Keyin's death. Fang fled in fear. Moments later he led his troops, shouting and clamoring, into the palace.

sentences.zh: 閩主聞變，匿於九龍帳下，亂兵刺之而出。

translations.literal: The ruler of Min heard of the upheaval, hid beneath the Nine Dragons canopy, and the mutinous soldiers stabbed him and dragged him out.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the upheaval, the ruler of Min hid beneath the Nine Dragons canopy. The mutinous soldiers stabbed him and dragged him out.

sentences.zh: 閩主宛轉未絕，宮人不忍其苦，為絕之。

translations.literal: The ruler of Min writhed and was not yet dead. The palace women could not bear his suffering and finished him off.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Min still writhed in agony. The palace women could not bear his suffering and ended his life.

sentences.zh: 倣與繼鵬殺陳后、陳守恩、陳匡勝、歸守明及繼鵬弟繼韜；

translations.literal: Fang and Jipeng killed Empress Chen, Chen Shou'en, Chen Kuangsheng, Gui Shouming, and Jipeng's younger brother Jitao.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Jipeng killed Empress Chen, Chen Shou'en, Chen Kuangsheng, Gui Shouming, and Jipeng's younger brother Jitao.

sentences.zh: 繼韜素與繼鵬相惡故也。

translations.literal: Jitao had long been mutually hostile with Jipeng; that was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao and Jipeng had long been enemies; that was why he was killed too.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，繼鵬稱皇太后令監國，是日，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On the day Xinsi, Jipeng, citing an order of the empress dowager, assumed regency over the state. That same day he ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day Jipeng, citing an order of the empress dowager, assumed regency. That same day he took the throne.

sentences.zh: 更名昶。

translations.literal: He changed his name to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name to Chang.

sentences.zh: 謚其父曰齊肅明孝皇帝，廟號惠宗。

translations.literal: He gave his father the posthumous title Emperor Qisu Mingxiao and the temple name Huizong.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously titled his father Emperor Qisu Mingxiao, with the temple name Huizong.

sentences.zh: 既而自稱權知福建節度事，遣使奉表於唐，大赦境內；

translations.literal: Thereafter he styled himself provisional administrator of the Fujian military commission, sent envoys to Tang with a memorial of submission, and proclaimed a general amnesty within his territory.
translations.idiomatic: He then styled himself provisional administrator of the Fujian military commission, sent envoys to Tang with a memorial of submission, and proclaimed a general amnesty within his realm.

sentences.zh: 立李春燕為賢妃。

translations.literal: He installed Li Chunyan as Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: He made Li Chunyan Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 初，閩惠宗娶漢主女清遠公主，使宦者閩清林延遇置邸於番禺，專掌國信。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huizong of Min married the Princess Qingyuan, daughter of the ruler of Han, and sent the eunuch Lin Yanyu of Minqing to establish a residence at Panyu, exclusively managing state correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Huizong of Min had married Princess Qingyuan, daughter of the ruler of Han, and sent the eunuch Lin Yanyu of Minqing to establish a residence at Panyu to manage state correspondence.

sentences.zh: 漢主賜以大第，稟賜甚厚，數問以閩事。

translations.literal: The ruler of Han bestowed on him a great mansion; stipends and gifts were very generous, and he repeatedly questioned him about affairs in Min.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Han granted him a great mansion and lavished stipends and gifts upon him, repeatedly questioning him about affairs in Min.

sentences.zh: 延遇不對，退，謂人曰：「去閩語閩，去越語越，處人宮禁，可如是乎！」

translations.literal: Yanyu did not reply. After withdrawing he said to someone: "Leave Min and speak of Min; leave Yue and speak of Yue—can one in another's palace precincts act like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanyu did not answer. After withdrawing he said, "Leave Min and speak of Min; leave Yue and speak of Yue—can one behave like this in another ruler's palace?"

sentences.zh: 漢主聞而賢之，以為內常侍，使鉤校諸司事。

translations.literal: The ruler of Han heard of it and considered him worthy, appointing him Inner Regular Attendant and having him audit the affairs of the various offices.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Han heard of this and admired him, appointing him Inner Regular Attendant and assigning him to audit the affairs of the various offices.

sentences.zh: 延遇聞惠宗遇弒，求歸，不許，素服向其國三日哭。

translations.literal: Yanyu heard that Huizong had met assassination, asked to return home, was not permitted, and in plain garb faced toward his state and mourned for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanyu learned that Huizong had been assassinated, he asked to return home but was refused. He put on mourning garb and wept toward Min for three days.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使高從誨，性明達，親禮賢士，委任梁震，以兄事之。

translations.literal: Gao Conghui, military commissioner of Jingnan, was by nature clear-sighted and penetrating. He personally honored worthy scholars, entrusted affairs to Liang Zhen, and treated him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Conghui, military commissioner of Jingnan, was clear-sighted by nature. He personally honored worthy scholars, entrusted affairs to Liang Zhen, and treated him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 震常謂從誨為郎君。

translations.literal: Zhen often addressed Conghui as "young master."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen often addressed Conghui as "young master."

sentences.zh: 楚王希範好奢靡，游談者共誇其盛，從誨謂僚佐曰：「如馬王可謂大丈夫矣。」

translations.literal: King Xi Fan of Chu loved extravagance. Those who wandered about in talk all praised his splendor together. Conghui said to his staff: "A lord like King Ma may truly be called a great man."
translations.idiomatic: King Xi Fan of Chu loved extravagance, and traveling gossips all praised his splendor. Conghui said to his staff, "A lord like King Ma may truly be called a great man."

sentences.zh: 孫光憲對曰：「天子諸侯，禮有等差。

translations.literal: Sun Guangxian replied: "The Son of Heaven and the feudal lords—ritual has gradations of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Guangxian replied, "The Son of Heaven and the feudal lords observe different ranks in ritual.

sentences.zh: 彼乳臭子驕侈僭□，取快一時，不為遠慮，危亡無日，又足慕乎！」

translations.literal: That milk-scented youth is arrogant, extravagant, and overreaching [—], seeking pleasure for a moment, making no far-sighted plans—ruin is not far off. What is there to admire!"
translations.idiomatic: That milk-scented boy is arrogant, extravagant, and overreaching his station, seeking pleasure for a moment with no thought for the future. His ruin is not far off. What is there to admire?"

sentences.zh: 從誨久而悟，曰：「公言是也。」

translations.literal: After a long while Conghui understood and said: "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Conghui understood and said, "Your words are right."

sentences.zh: 它日，謂梁震曰：「吾自念平生奉養，固已過矣。」

translations.literal: On another day he said to Liang Zhen: "Reflecting on my lifelong maintenance and support, it is already excessive."
translations.idiomatic: On another day he said to Liang Zhen, "Looking back on how I have lived all my life, I have already gone too far."

sentences.zh: 乃捐去玩好，以經史自娛，省刑薄賦，境內以安。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cast aside amusements and curiosities, took the classics and histories for his own pleasure, reduced punishments and lightened taxes, and within his territory there was peace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he cast aside amusements and curiosities, took comfort in the classics and histories, reduced punishments and lightened taxes, and brought peace to his realm.

sentences.zh: 梁震曰：「先王待我如布衣交，以嗣王屬我。

translations.literal: Liang Zhen said: "The former king treated me like a commoner's friendship and entrusted the heir to me.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhen said, "The former king treated me as a friend among common men and entrusted the heir to my care.

sentences.zh: 今嗣王能自立，不墜其業，吾老矣，不復事人矣。」

translations.literal: Now the heir can stand on his own and does not let the enterprise fall. I am old and will no longer serve others."
translations.idiomatic: Now the heir can stand on his own and has not let the enterprise fall. I am old and will serve no other master."

sentences.zh: 遂固請退居。

translations.literal: Thereupon he firmly requested to withdraw and retire.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he firmly asked to withdraw and retire.

sentences.zh: 從誨不能留，乃為之築室於士洲。

translations.literal: Conghui could not keep him and therefore built him a dwelling on Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Conghui could not keep him and built him a dwelling on Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 震披鶴氅，自稱荊台隱士，每詣府，跨黃牛至聽事。

translations.literal: Zhen wore a crane-feather cloak, styled himself Hermit of Jing Terrace, and whenever he went to the headquarters rode a yellow ox to the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen wore a crane-feather cloak, styled himself Hermit of Jing Terrace, and whenever he visited the headquarters rode a yellow ox to the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 從誨時過其家，四時賜與甚厚。

translations.literal: Conghui often visited his home, and seasonal gifts and grants were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Conghui often visited his home and lavished seasonal gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 自是悉以政事屬孫光憲。

translations.literal: From this time onward he entrusted all governmental affairs to Sun Guangxian.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he entrusted all governmental affairs to Sun Guangxian.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：「孫光憲見微而能諫，高從誨聞善而能徙，梁震成功而能退，自古有國家者能如是，夫何亡國敗家喪身之有。」

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: "Sun Guangxian perceived subtle signs and was able to remonstrate; Gao Conghui heard what was good and was able to change; Liang Zhen achieved success and was able to withdraw. Since antiquity, those who possessed a state and were able to be like this—how could there be loss of state, ruin of family, or death of person!"
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Guang observes: "Sun Guangxian saw the first signs and was able to remonstrate; Gao Conghui heard what was good and was able to change; Liang Zhen achieved success and was able to withdraw. Since antiquity, rulers who could act thus—how could they lose their states, ruin their families, or forfeit their lives?"

sentences.zh: 吳加中書令徐知誥尚父、太師、大丞相、大元帥，進封齊王，備殊禮，以升、潤、宣、池、歙、常、江、饒、信、海十州為齊國；

translations.literal: Wu added for Chief Councillor Xu Zhigao the titles Exalted Father, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chief Councillor, and Grand Marshal, advanced his enfeoffment to Prince of Qi, granted extraordinary honors, and made the ten prefectures Sheng, Run, Xuan, Chi, She, Chang, Jiang, Rao, Xin, and Hai into the state of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu added for Chief Councillor Xu Zhigao the titles Exalted Father, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chief Councillor, and Grand Marshal, advanced his enfeoffment to Prince of Qi, granted him extraordinary honors, and made the ten prefectures of Sheng, Run, Xuan, Chi, She, Chang, Jiang, Rao, Xin, and Hai into the state of Qi.

sentences.zh: 知誥辭尚父、丞相，殊禮不受。

translations.literal: Zhigao declined the titles Exalted Father and Chief Councillor and did not accept the extraordinary honors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao declined the titles Exalted Father and Chief Councillor and refused the extraordinary honors.

sentences.zh: 閩皇城使、判六軍諸衛李倣專制朝政，陰養死士，閩主昶與拱宸指揮使林延皓等圖之。

translations.literal: Li Fang, commissioner of the Imperial City and administrator of the Six Armies and the various guards in Min, monopolized court governance and secretly maintained death-fighters. The ruler of Min, Chang, together with Lin Yanhao, commander of the Gongchen Guard, and others plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang, commissioner of the Imperial City and administrator of the Six Armies and various guards in Min, monopolized court governance and secretly maintained death-fighters. The ruler of Min, Chang, together with Gongchen Guard commander Lin Yanhao and others, plotted against him.

sentences.zh: 延皓等詐親附倣，倣待之不疑。

translations.literal: Yanhao and the others feigned closeness and attachment to Fang; Fang treated them without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhao and the others feigned loyalty to Fang, and Fang trusted them completely.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬子，倣入朝，延皓等伏衛士數百於內殿，執斬之，梟首朝門。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day Renzi, Fang entered court. Yanhao and the others hid several hundred guards in the inner hall, seized him and beheaded him, and displayed his head at the court gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the renzi day, Fang entered court. Yanhao and the others hid several hundred guards in the inner hall, seized and beheaded him, and displayed his head at the court gate.

sentences.zh: 倣部兵千餘持白梃攻應天門，不克，焚啟聖門，奪倣首奔吳越。

translations.literal: More than a thousand of Fang's troops, bearing white clubs, attacked the Gate of Responding to Heaven but did not succeed. They burned the Gate of Initiating Sagacity, seized Fang's head, and fled to Wu-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand of Fang's troops, bearing white clubs, attacked the Gate of Responding to Heaven but failed. They burned the Gate of Initiating Sagacity, seized Fang's head, and fled to Wu-Yue.

sentences.zh: 詔暴倣弒君及殺繼韜等罪，告諭中外。

translations.literal: An edict publicly exposed Fang's crimes of regicide and killing Jitao and the others, and announced this within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict publicly exposed Fang's crimes of regicide and the killing of Jitao and others, and announced them throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 以建王繼嚴權判六軍諸衛，以六軍判官永泰葉翹為內宣徽使、參政事。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian Jiyan was appointed provisional administrator of the Six Armies and various guards. Ye Qiao of Yongtai, judge of the Six Armies, was made Inner Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiyan of Jian was appointed provisional administrator of the Six Armies and various guards. Ye Qiao of Yongtai, judge of the Six Armies, was made Inner Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and participant in governance.

sentences.zh: 翹博學質直，閩惠宗擢為福王友，昶以師傅禮待之，多所裨益，宮中謂之「國翁」。

translations.literal: Qiao was broadly learned and plain-spoken. Huizong of Min promoted him to be tutor to the Prince of Fu. Chang treated him with the rites due a master and tutor, and he was of much benefit. Within the palace he was called "Grandfather of the State."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was broadly learned and plain-spoken. Huizong of Min had promoted him to tutor the Prince of Fu. Chang treated him with the rites due a master and tutor, and benefited greatly from his counsel. Within the palace he was called "Grandfather of the State."

sentences.zh: 昶既嗣位，驕縱，不與翹議國事。

translations.literal: After Chang succeeded to the throne, he was arrogant and unrestrained and did not discuss state affairs with Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chang succeeded to the throne, he grew arrogant and unrestrained and no longer consulted Qiao on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 一旦，昶方視事，翹衣道士服過庭中趨出，昶召還，拜之，曰：「軍國事殷，久不接對，孤之過也。」

translations.literal: One day, as Chang was just conducting business, Qiao, dressed in Taoist robes, passed through the courtyard and hurried out. Chang summoned him back, bowed to him, and said: "Military and state affairs are pressing. It has been long since we met in audience—this is my fault."
translations.idiomatic: One day, as Chang was conducting business, Qiao, dressed in Taoist robes, passed through the courtyard and hurried out. Chang summoned him back, bowed to him, and said, "Military and state affairs are pressing. It has been long since we met—this is my fault."

sentences.zh: 翹頓首曰：「老臣輔導無狀，致陛下即位以來無一善可稱，願乞骸骨。」

translations.literal: Qiao prostrated himself and said: "This old minister's guidance has been without merit, causing that since Your Majesty's accession not one good deed can be named. I wish to request my bones."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao prostrated himself and said, "This old minister's guidance has been without merit, so that since Your Majesty's accession not one good deed can be named. I beg to resign my post."

sentences.zh: 昶曰：「先帝以孤屬公，政令不善，公當極言，奈何棄孤去！」

translations.literal: Chang said: "The former emperor entrusted me to you. If the government orders are not good, you should speak to the utmost—how can you abandon me and leave!"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "The former emperor entrusted me to your care. If my orders are wrong, you should speak plainly—how can you abandon me!"

sentences.zh: 厚賜金帛，慰諭令復位。

translations.literal: He richly bestowed gold and silk, comforted and instructed him, and ordered him to resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: He richly rewarded him with gold and silk, comforted him, and ordered him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 昶元妃梁國夫人李氏，同平章事敏之女，昶嬖李春燕，待夫人甚薄。

translations.literal: Chang's primary consort was Lady Li, Madame of the State of Liang, daughter of Co-Grand Councillor Min. Chang favored Li Chunyan and treated the lady very coldly.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's primary consort was Lady Li, Madame of the State of Liang, daughter of Co-Grand Councillor Min. Chang favored Li Chunyan and treated his consort very coldly.

sentences.zh: 翹諫曰：「夫人先帝之甥，聘之以禮，奈何以新愛而棄之！」

translations.literal: Qiao remonstrated, saying: "The lady is the former emperor's niece. She was betrothed by ritual—how can you cast her aside because of a new favorite!"
translations.idiomatic: Qiao remonstrated, saying, "The lady is the former emperor's niece. She was betrothed with proper ceremony—how can you cast her aside for a new favorite!"

sentences.zh: 昶不說，由是疏之。

translations.literal: Chang was displeased and from this grew distant from him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was displeased and from then on kept his distance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復上書言事，昶批其紙尾曰：「一葉隨風落御溝。」

translations.literal: Before long he again submitted a memorial on affairs. Chang wrote on the end of the paper: "One leaf follows the wind and falls into the imperial ditch."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Qiao submitted another memorial. Chang wrote on the margin, "One leaf follows the wind and falls into the imperial ditch."

sentences.zh: 遂放歸永泰，以壽終。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was released to return to Yongtai and ended his life in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was sent home to Yongtai, where he died of old age.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉馬全節之功，召詣闕。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Ma Quanjie's achievement and summoned him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Ma Quanjie's achievement and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 劉延朗求賂，全節無以與之；

translations.literal: Liu Yanlang sought a bribe, but Quanjie had nothing to give him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanlang demanded a bribe, but Quanjie had nothing to give him.

sentences.zh: 延朗欲除全節絳州刺史，群議沸騰。

translations.literal: Yanlang wished to remove Quanjie to the post of prefect of Jiang Prefecture, and public discussion seethed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang wanted to demote Quanjie to prefect of Jiangzhou, and outrage spread through the court.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，乙卯，以全節為橫海留後。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it. On the day Yimao, Quanjie was appointed acting military commissioner of Henghai.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, on the yimao day he appointed Quanjie acting military commissioner of Henghai.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬申，以中書侍郎、同平章事充樞密使韓昭胤同平章事，充護國節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day Renshen, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councillor, concurrently Palace Secretariat Commissioner Han Zhaoyin, was made Co-Grand Councillor and Huguo Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day Renshen, Han Zhaoyin, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councillor who also served as Palace Secretariat Commissioner, was made Co-Grand Councillor and military commissioner of Huguo.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以前匡國節度使、同平章事馮道為司空。

translations.literal: On the day Yiyou former Kuangguo Military Commissioner and Co-Grand Councillor Feng Dao was made Grand Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yiyou, Feng Dao, former military commissioner of Kuangguo and Co-Grand Councillor, was made Grand Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 時久無正拜三公者，朝議疑其職事；

translations.literal: For a long time there had been no regular appointment to the Three Excellencies, and court discussion doubted what his duties should be;
translations.idiomatic: For a long time there had been no regular appointment to the Three Excellencies, and court discussion doubted what his duties should be.

sentences.zh: 盧文紀欲令掌祭祀掃除，道聞之曰：「司空掃除，職也，吾何憚焉。」

translations.literal: Lu Wenji wished to have him in charge of sweeping at sacrifices; when Dao heard this he said, "Sweeping is the Grand Master of Works' duty—what is there for me to fear."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenji wished to have him in charge of sweeping at sacrifices. When Dao heard this he said, "Sweeping is the Grand Master of Works' duty. What is there for me to fear?"

sentences.zh: 既而文紀自知不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Before long Wenji knew himself it would not do, and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wenji knew it would not do and stopped.

sentences.zh: 閩主賜洞真先生陳守元號天師，信重之，乃至更易將相、刑罰、選舉，皆與之議；

translations.literal: The ruler of Min gave Master Dongzhen Chen Shouyuan the title Heavenly Master, trusted and honored him, and even in changing generals and ministers, punishments, and selections—all was discussed with him;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Min gave Master Dongzhen Chen Shouyuan the title Heavenly Master, trusted and honored him, and even in changing generals and ministers, punishments, and selections—all was discussed with him.

sentences.zh: 守元受賂請托，言無不從，其門如市。

translations.literal: Shouyuan accepted bribes and requests for favor; none of his words went unheeded, and his gate was like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyuan accepted bribes and requests for favor. None of his words went unheeded, and his gate was like a market.
